With the mantra, "You two are wealth and you are lovely" (KS 39.1:118.14–15; ApŚS 16.33.1), he places those two to the north with the mantra, "Of the god... sit ye firm" (ibid., omitting *tejase vām* and following the Taittirīya version).

With the formula, “Take refuge in heaven; strive in the intermediate space” (TS 5.6.10.1; cf. KS 39.1:118.17–18), he places a *caru* offering for Bṛhaspati in the midst of these very four [bricks], with the formula, “Be united with the earth; sit down with her” (ibid. o, 2 & T mantra). Into those [bricks], as they have been laid, he scatters chips of gold with the formulas, “For you two, for brilliance; for you two, for light; for you two, for semen; for you two, for luster; for you two, for life; for you two, for offspring” (cf. the omitted words in the above KS = Ap mantra).

With the words, "Thou art the splendor of sacred knowledge" (5.6.10,3), he pours [the oblation] into the sacrificial porridge for Bṛhaspati (bārhaspatya-caru). Standing to the west of the junction of the tail at the time of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick, while reciting the hymn to the Waters (*apām stotra*), he worships with this section of the text beginning, "Golden-hued, pure, purifying" (5.6.1a,1). Having stepped out to the sacrificial ground (*vihāra*), he gazes upon the porridge for Bṛhaspati with the formula, "For the sake of the splendor of sacred knowledge, thee! (cf. the end of 5.6.1).

With the words, “Thou art the back of the waters” (4.2.8c,1), he takes up a lotus leaf; with “The womb of Agni, swelling around the ocean” (*ibid.* 2), and “Increasing” (*ibid.* 3), he spreads it out;

with “Spread forth as greatness” (*ibid.*, to the end), and “That art thou, the Truth, the womb of heat” (?), he places it at the time for the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks, turned upward and facing eastward. With “By that—” (*tayā*)... [he continues].

With the *tayādevata* formula, "Sit down," he places a gold plate (*rukmam*) upon that [altar], with its raised rim facing north, using the verse beginning "The Brahman was born" (4.2.8d,1). Then, with the verse "First in front...

shine forth" (ibid., to the end), and the *tayādevata* formula, he sprinkles [the gold plate] diagonally with five portions of ghee taken in five ladlings, while reciting the five verses beginning "Make your body wide like a plain" (1.2.14a,1–e; cf. BSS 10.30:8–9).

With the verse, "Hiraṇyagarbha arose in the beginning" (TS 4.2.8e,1), he places upon that [altar] a golden man to the south, facing east and lying supine. He touches him with the mantra, "The Lord of what has been born... let us worship with oblation; by that deity, sit down" (from the same text to the end, followed by the *tayādevata* formula), and with the verse, "The drop fell... through the earth and heaven... the seven priests; by that deity, sit down" (from the same text to the end, followed by the *tayādevata* formula). (TS 4.2.8f,1) (M262)

He offers a fourfold-drawn portion at the mouth of the verse: “*Prajāpati moves within the womb*; being born, he is born in many ways—this the wise poets perceive (*paripaśyanti*) through their insights, *svāhā*. “Recite the *śāman*,” he says. The *prastotṛ* recites the *puruṣasāman*.

"Thrice-threefold is your head, O Agni," with these words he worships him: "That is my head, O Agni. Fifteenfold is your wing, O Agni; that is my wing, O Agni. Seventeenfold is your wing, O Agni; that is my wing, O Agni. Twenty-one-fold is your tail, O Agni; that is my tail, O Agni. Twenty-five-fold is your self, O Agni; that is my self, O Agni. Twenty-seven-fold are your two thighs, O Agni; those are my two thighs, O Agni. Thirty-three-fold is your [body], O Agni."

"That stability is mine, O Agni; that stability is mine"—with these words, at a distance of one cubit to the south, he stretches out a ladle made of *kārṣmarya* wood, filled with clarified butter, over the naturally perforated brick (*svayamātṛṇṇā*), saying: "I place you with the brilliance of Agni," and "I place you with the mind"; he places it with his mind, saying: "With her, sit down" (the *tayā devatā* formula).

With the Gāyatrī verse, "Agni is the head" (4.4.4a), he touches [the earth]; with "He quickens the sky... by that sit thou" (ibid., end) and the *tayā devatā* formula, he places an Udumbara post full of curds, measuring exactly one cubit (*aratni*), to the north of the place where the naturally perforated brick (*svayamātṛṇṇā*) was laid; the post made of Kārṣmarya wood remains unplaced.

Then the Adhvaryu distributes the *arka* wood. Having explained the *saptahotṛ* formula over the ladle made of *kārṣmarya* wood, he takes [the fire] from the *kārṣmarya* ladle with the *sruva* spoon into the *audumbara* ladle; he brings that into the *audumbara* ladle. Having explained the *daśahotṛ* formula over the *audumbara* ladle, he takes the *kārṣmarya* ladle from the *audumbara* ladle with the *sruva* spoon at the offering of the *daśahotṛ*;
he brings that into the *kārṣmarya* ladle. He carries it an odd number of times and establishes it facing north.

"Thus many years shall be very auspicious," so the Adhvaryu should say after having offered the *arka* oblation, and he should arrange it according to the *ṛc*. With the formula, "For the sake of the year—with Indra’s power I place thee," he places it mentally.

With the *tayā devatā* mantra, "Sit with that," and with the *triṣṭubh* verse, "Bhuvaḥ... (4.4.4d), he touches it. Then with the formula, "Of the sacrifice... the bearer of oblations, sit with that" (from the same passage to the end, followed by the *tayā devatā* mantra).
At this very point, he mutters the *sarpa-yajus* formulas: "Homage be to the serpents" (TS 4.2.8.1), and "Homage to those serpents who lie anywhere" (ibid.).

With the formula "Bhūr! Vāk! Āyuḥ! he takes up the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick. [He then places] the *ṛc* and the clarified butter... [he causes the horse to smell] the *ṛc*s with the formula: "Being well-disposed, may Agni and Agni, coming together in procreation, the two givers of jewels, the pair of milch-cows, yield milk for me without faltering. (TS 5.1.9.3–4)

He gives her to the Brahman priest with the words, “May he give to me. The Brahman accepts her with the words, “May Agni grant me the senses, vigor, great power, and glory—the thirty-three heroic strengths. He takes the fire into himself with the words, “O Brahman... you are power. He puts on a leather sandal with the word “ascend,” and he ascends by means of the mounting. Or rather, having taken hold of her together with this [sandals], he places them down; thus it is said.

Reciting the *yajus* formula, "Thou art firm, a supporter, spread out" (TS 4.2.9a), both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer say, "With the most peaceful shelter of Viśvakarman, with that, sit down" (ibid. a to the end & b).
Having laid this brick down with the syllable "bhūḥ," he breathes over it.
The sacrificer gives a choice gift to the Adhvaryu, and the Adhvaryu gives it to the Pratiprasthātṛ.

The Pratiprasthātṛ, for whatever desire he may have, steps upon her with his two thumbs while reciting, “I have stepped upon the earth” (5.6.8.1a1,1). With the words, “May breath not forsake me” (ibid., 2), and “I offer consciousness” (5.5.4.3), he offers four ladlings of ghee upon her, concluding with, “With mind and ghee—svāhā! (ibid., to the end). He says, “Recite the *śamyu*! The Prastotṛ addresses the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks.

With the mantra, "Thou art splendor" (*tejo 'si*), he places a gold brick (*hiraṇyeṣṭakā*) upon this [earth-brick], saying: "Bestow splendor upon me; protect me from the earth. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras" (ibid., with the *T* mantra).
(Note:
This passage concerns the eight *ṣaṃyānī* bricks and the *Zīrṣaṇya* bricks.)

[He places two *dūrvā* bricks, touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick, with the preceding formula: “From joint to joint they sprout” (TS 4.2.9c,1). With the formula beginning “And with a hundred joints... by that deity... you who extend with a hundred” (from *ibid.* c to the end; the *T-mantra* and *ibid.* d,1), he places one to the north.
With the formula beginning “With a thousand... through the oblation... by that [deity]... sit down” (from *ibid.* d to the end and the *tayādevata* mantra), he places the other.

With the mantra, "Those splendors of yours which are in the sun" (4.2.9n,1), he places above those two the *vāmabhṛt* brick, which has two *yajus*-formulas and a golden head, with the formula, "Lifted up... do thou make" (ibid., end), followed by the deity-mantra, "O gods, that which you... (4.2.9o), and "O Bṛhaspati... (4.2.9o), followed by the placement-mantra, "By that deity... sit thou" (4.2.9n + T-mantra & ibid. o + T-mantra).
With the mantra, "The Virāj held the light" (4.2.9p1), he places that *virāj* brick to the east, with the formula, "By that... sit thou" (T-mantra).

With the formula, “Thou art Virāj, the seed-shedder,” he places the *retassic* brick to its south, [saying]: “In the *śāma* pour the seed; in the *śāma* place the seed; in the *śāma* generate the seed. Through thee may he conquer this world; sit down with her. (BaudhŚS 10.31:29.12–3).

With the formula, “May Bṛhaspati seat thee” (4.4.6a,1), he places the Viśvajyotis brick with the preceding one, [saying]: “On the back of the earth, luminous, bestow universal light for every out-breath and in-breath; Agni is thy overlord; with that [brick], sit thou firm” (ibid., to the end & T-mantra).

With the formula, “Thou art the invincible Aṣāḍhā, the subduer” (4.2.9e,1), he places the Tryālikhita bricks with the preceding one, [saying]: “Subdue the enemies, subdue those who oppose us; inspire us; with that [brick], sit thou firm” (ibid., to the end & T-mantra). These have their marks facing north.

"Madhuś ca mādhvaś ca"—with this [formula], he places those two [bricks] as the seasonal ones (*ṛtavye*) according to the preceding [rule]: "The two spring seasons; you are the internal bond of Agni; may heaven and earth, the two spring seasons, being well-disposed, settle around Indra, just as the gods [settled around him]; by that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit firm! (4.4.11g & Tmantra). Thus [ends the section from 4.4.11a to the end, and 4.4.11g & Tmantra].

With the verse, “O Agni, those moist wombs of yours,” he places a reed-grass stalk (*avakā*) along [the bricks]. With the formula, “Those which are nest-like; being in harmony with all of them, perceiving [them], sit here for the sake of the body—with that [deity]—sit” (as cited above and in the *Tmantra*;

cf. *Agni* tr., p. 543, n. 80, end), he extends eight *saṃyānī* bricks to the east of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *haṃsapātinī* verses toward the north: “Thou art the paths of Agni; by that deity... (4.4.6e, 1 with the *Tmantra*). (M265)

O Agni, those which are yours among the gods, by that deity (with the *T* mantra as in ibid. e.2); O Vāyu, those which are yours, by that deity (with the *T* mantra as in ibid. f.1); O Vāyu, those which are yours among the gods, by that deity (with the *T* mantra as in ibid. f.2); those which are yours in the intermediate space, by that deity (with the *T* mantra as in ibid. g.1); those which are yours among the gods in the intermediate space, by that deity (with the *T* mantra as in ibid. g.2); you are the intermediate space, by that [deity].

With the mantra "For the deity thee" (ibid., 1 with the T-mantra) and "For the intermediate space thee; with that one, sit down" (ibid., 2 with the T-mantra), he places the companion brick to the east with the mantra: "I yoke thee as a companion for Indra and Agni; with that one, sit down" (4.4.5a1 & the T-mantra; regarding the ritual application of 4.4.5a, see BSS Tr. p. 543 n. 79).

He spreads nine [bricks] on the head towards the east, behind the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stones, three by three, facing westward. While they face westward, he makes him recite; he establishes them facing northward with three [mantras]: "Indro dadhīco asthabhiḥ... nine... with that deity," "Icchan aśvasya... Nāvati... with that deity," and "Atrāha go... gṛhe... with that deity—sit! (TB 1.5.8.1–3). Thus, there are three.
"Indram it r anūṣata—by that deity; indra id dharyo hiraṇyayaḥ—by that deity; indra vājeṣu ūtibhiḥ—by that deity, sit down"—these are three [verses].

"Tam indraṃ vājayāmasi—may he be present, by that deity; indraḥ sadamane saumyaḥ—by that deity; girā vajro astṛtaḥ—by that deity, sit down"—[these are the others], with the *T* mantra for each. (TB 1.5.8.1–3 [4, 5, 7], with the *T* mantra for each). Thus.

He follows this with the *sūdadohas* verse: "Those [waters] of his, yielding sweetness... (VS 4.2.4). Having placed one brick with the mantra "sit down with that," he should recite over it: "By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit ye two firmly" (VS T-mantra); and with "By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit ye firmly" (VS T-mantra), he places many bricks.

He takes up the tortoise and anoints it with curds mixed with honey while reciting the three verses, "The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order" (4.2.9g–i). He recites, "Honey flow from the cows; may they be ours" (ibid.
g, 2–i), and "May the great heaven and earth be for us" (4.2.9k, 1) as he wipes its sides. Then he recites, "This sacrifice [we offer] with our invocations" (ibid. to the end).

With the formula, “I set thee down upon the navel of the earth,” he places it to the north. Then, while the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick has been turned westward in front of the tortoise, he mutters the *yajus*: “May the sun not terrify thee... O men, with unbroken wings, forward...”

"Look upon [them]; may the divine rain follow you! O bull of the waters, lord of bricks, cross over the three oceans that lead to heaven. Go there where the ancients have departed, clothing yourself in the *purīṣa*, to the world of the doers of good.
Having turned him toward the east, he lays it down with the mantra: "Sit with that. (Tmantra)
"Let the four quarters proceed, O fires," [with this they... *svāhā*—thus they firmly establish [the enclosing sticks]. "Satiated, [grant] wisdom, vigor, food, and imperishability."

Having placed a tortoise made of *udumbara* wood in a mortar made of *udumbara* wood, and having thrown rice and barley into it, he threshes them while reciting: "Thou art the portion of vigor" (*ūrjo bhāgo 'si*). He then sets that very thing down with the formula: "Thou art the source of vigor; bestow vigor upon me, the sacrificer; sit here with her" (*ūrjo janitram ūrjam mahyaṃ yajamānāya dhehi tayāsīda*). He places the *viṣṇusala* stone along with it, reciting: "O Viṣṇu, by this... and so on, ending with: "...sit here with her" (*...tayāsīda*).
"Sewn with nectar, O Goddess, you have come," [with these words] he places the fire-pan (*ukhā*) behind the mortar (*ulūkhala*).

"The pan, the sister, has stood upon the altar, longing for the truth that was first made known by the seers; may Agni, the wise one, perform that here. O Earth, sit upon the earth, upon the back of the Mother. (MS 2.7.16:100.14–16; KS 39.3:121.19f.)

"Thou art firm, O earth; overcome those who attack us; thou art sewn together by the gods with immortality; sit down with her"—with this [formula], standing toward the east over it, he makes an offering with four ladlings of ghee, [reciting] "O Agni, yoke those that are thine... (4.2.9q,1) up to "...the swift horses... svāhā" (ibid., to the end, with *svāhā*).
With the verse, “Harness the steeds that best invoke the gods” (4.2.9r,1), he takes another fourfold portion while sitting facing west. With the formula, “The horse, O Agni... sit down, svāhā!
(ibid., ending with *svāhā*), he takes up the head of the man.

Into its mouth, he throws a piece of gold with the verse, “A drop has fallen” (4.2.9s,1). [Into the nostrils, he places two pieces of gold. With the formula, “[Along] the earth... the invocations” (ibid., to the end), he places [the gold].
With the mantra, "This has become the vigor of the entire world" (4.2.9t,1), he places [the gold plate] on the right vital breath; with "Of Agni Vaiśvānara" (ibid. 2), on the left;
with "Agni is radiant with light" (ibid. 3), on the right temple; and with "The golden disk is resplendent with luster" (ibid.
4), on the left. With "For the Ṛc, thee! (4.2.9u,1), he places it on the right ear; and with "For radiance, thee! (ibid. 2), on the left.

With the verse, “The streams flow peacefully like milch-cows” (TS 4.2.9.1), he fills [the vessel] with curds mixed with honey. With the verse, “Within the heart, a stream of immortality” (TS 4.2.9.2),

he places [the mixture] into the fire-pan (*ukhā*), which is turned upward and facing east, while reciting, “Anointing the solar embryo with milk” (TS 4.2.10.1) and “Of the thousand being built” (ibid.).
With the verse, "Do not harm this one" (4.2.10b), he releases his grief. With the mantra, "Settle down as a two-footed one;

sit with her" (Taitt. Ār. 10.1.10), and with the two verses beginning "Upwards that Jātavedas" (1.4.43a, occurring many times in the Taittirīya Śruti texts), he twice offers two portions of four-drawn ghee together over it, concluding with, "They carry the god Sūrya, svāhā! (1.4.43a, with *svāhā*).

With the mantra, "Viśvakarman is the lord of the quarters" (5.5.5,1), he places a piece of gold. With the mantra, "To him who [is] our cattle, obeisance; sit with her" (ibid., to the end & T mantra), and with "The course of Vāta, the navel of Varuṇa" (4.2.10c,1), he places the head of the horse facing westward in front, at the end of his own body, with the mantra, "The horse being born in the expanse of the flood" (ibid., to the end).

Having touched the human head with the mantra, “The sun is the embryo” (4.2.10a,1), he releases its heat with the mantra, “Do not harm this one” (4.2.10d,1). Then, with the mantra, “Of single-hoofed animals, [the wild] is the Gaura; sit down, sit down with her” (ibid., end of section & T mantra), he places a piece of gold into this [mantra], “Prajāpati is the lord of the quarters” (5.5.5.1,2), with the words, “...to us, homage; sit down, sit down with her” (ibid., end of section & T mantra).

With the verse, "The unceasing, red, and restless drop" (4.2.10e), he places the head of the bull facing eastward at the rear, at the edge of his own body. Having touched the head of the Puruṣa with the verses, "I praise Agni, the first... (ibid., to the end), and "The Aditya, the embryo" (4.2.10a), he releases its pain with the verse, "This ocean... (4.2.10f), ending with: "...the hundred-streamed one in the sky, O Gavaya, sit down;
with that, sit down" (ibid., to the end & T mantra).

With the formula, "Rudra is the lord of the quarters" (ŚB 5.5.5.1), he places a piece of gold; with "May he protect our cattle—homage! Sit down with her" (ibid.), he places the head of a bull, turned toward the north, on the south side with the formula, "The protector of the enclosure, the navel of Tvaṣṭṛ and Varuṇa" (TS 4.2.10g).

At the end of the *ātman* [fire], having touched the sun with the verse, "The one who was born from the non-existent in the space of the mid-region" (ibid.), he releases its heat with the verse, "This woolly one" (4.2.10h). With the mantra, "O camel, wild, dwelling in the space of Varuṇa, sit down; sit down with her" (ibid.

& T mantra), and with the mantra, "Varuṇa is the lord of the quarters" (5.5.5.1), he places a piece of gold [on the fire] with the mantra, "May he protect our cattle... homage; sit down with her" (ibid. & T mantra).
With the verse, "The fire which was born from the heat of Agni" (4.2.10.i.1), he places the head of a goat on the north side, turning toward the south at the edge of his own body;

then, having touched the head of the man with the mantra, "The womb of Aditi" (4.2.10a.1), he releases its heat with the mantra, "For the goat is indeed of Agni" (4.2.10k.1), ending with, "It was born... [K1,K4,58a11] ...it went to the wild Śarabha... sit down, sit with her" (ibid.).

At the mantra, “Agni is the lord of the quarters” (ŚB 5.5.1.5), he places a piece of gold with the formula: “Be seated here through that [brick] which is homage” (ibid., end of section & Taittirīya mantra).
These are the *Apasyā* (15), the *Chandasyā* (5), the *Prāṇabhṛt* (50), and the *Apānabhṛt* (50) bricks.
Cf. Akh. <24>, <25>, pp. 617–620 on the *Prāṇabhṛt-* and *Apānabhṛt-* bricks.

He spreads fifteen *apasyā* bricks on all sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*: five in the east, five in the south, five in the west, and five in the north; these are the *cchandasyā* bricks, and they are laid down diagonally, one by one, surrounding each *svayamātṛṇṇā*.

In the *samīcī* bricks, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "I settle thee in the out-breath" (4.3.1a,1)—with this he places one in front; "by that deity, I settle thee in the down-breath" (ibid. a,2 & T mantra); "by that deity, I settle thee in the ash" (ibid. a,3 & T mantra); "by that deity, I settle thee in the light" (ibid. a,4 & T mantra); "by that deity, I settle thee in the path" (ibid.
a,5 & T mantra)—thus [he proceeds with each, using the respective T-mantra]. (4.3.1a,1–5).

"Apān tvā sadane sādayāmi"—thus [he says] behind; "tayā devatayā, apān tvā sadhasthe sādayāmi, tayā devatayā, apān tvā purīṣe sādayāmi, tayā devatayā, apān tvā yonau sādayāmi, tayā devatayā, apān tvā pāthasi sādayāmi, tayā... sīda"—thus [he says], with the respective *T-mantras* for each (4.3.1c, 1–5).

"Sit in the ocean as your seat"—thus [he places it] to the south. "By that deity (with the *T* mantra), sit in the sea as your seat; by that deity (ibid. b, 2 with the *T* mantra), sit in the water as your seat; by that deity (ibid. b, 3 with the *T* mantra), sit in the abode of the waters; by that deity, sit in the gathering-place of the waters"—thus [he places it]. (Cf. 4.3.1b, 4–5 with the *T* mantras in the lacunae).

"To the Gāyatrī metre" (4.3.1d, 1)—thus [he places it] to the north; "by that deity (with the T-mantra), to the Triṣṭubh metre; by that deity (as above, d, 2 and T-mantra), to the Jagatī metre; by that deity (as above, d, 3 with T-mantra), to the Anuṣṭubh metre; by that deity (as above, d, 4 with T-mantra), to the Paṅkti metre; by that deity—sit! (as above, d, 5 with T-mantra). Thus.

He spreads fifty life-supporting bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks—ten in each of the directions. Ten [bricks] go around to the south of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*. They are laid down touching [the *svayamātṛṇṇā*] diagonally. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *śamīcī* bricks.

With the formula, “This one is *purobhuvaḥ*,” he places it in front. [The text continues: “By that deity, his breath is *bhauvāyana*; by that deity, spring is *prāṇāyana*; by that deity, the *gāyatrī* belongs to spring; by that deity, the *gāyatra* chant belongs to the *gāyatrī*; by that deity, the *upāṃśu* cup belongs to the *gāyatra*... (and so on, as per the respective sections).

[With the mantra: "Of the *upāṃśu* [cup] there is the *trivṛt* [stoma]; by that [stoma], [the *rathaṃtara* (sāman)]; from the *rathaṃtara*, the seer Vasiṣṭha; by that [seer], O you who are grasped by Prajāpati, I grasp the breath for the sake of offspring; by that, sit down" (4.3.2a,1–10, with the respective *Taittirīya* mantra for each).

"This one behind is Viśvavyacas" (4.3.2c,1). Behind it: "With that"—[Taittirīya mantra]—"his eye is the Viśvavyacas; 'with that' (ibid. c,2 with T mantra), the rainy seasons are those belonging to the eye; 'with that' (ibid. c,3 with T mantra), the Jagatī meter belongs to the rainy seasons; 'with that' (ibid. c,4 and T mantra), from the Jagatī comes the Ṛkṣama; 'with that' (ibid. c,5 with T mantra), from the Ṛkṣama comes the Śukra; 'with that' (ibid. c,6 with T mantra)."

From Śukra [comes] the seventeenfold [stoma], with that [verse] (ibid. c, 7 with its respective *Taittirīya* mantra); from the seventeenfold [comes] the Vairūpa [sāman], with that [verse] (ibid. c, 8 with its respective *Taittirīya* mantra); from the Vairūpa [comes] the seer Viśvāmitra, with that [verse] (ibid. c, 9 with its respective *Taittirīya* mantra); "With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the eye for all creatures; with that [verse], sit down" (ibid. c, 10 & its respective *Taittirīya* mantra) (4.3.2c, 1–10, with the *Taittirīya* mantra for each).

"This one to the south is Viśvakarman" (4.3.2b,1)—thus [he places it] to the south. "By that... (Taittirīya mantra); his mind belongs to Viśvakarman. "By that... (ibid. b,2 with Taittirīya mantra); summer is [the season] of the mind. "By that... (ibid. b,3 with Taittirīya mantra); the *triṣṭubh* meter belongs to summer. "By that... (ibid. b,4 with Taittirīya mantra); the *aiḍa* chant belongs to the *triṣṭubh*. "By that... (ibid. b,5 with Taittirīya mantra); from the *aiḍa* comes the *antaryāma* cup. "By that... (ibid. b,6 with Taittirīya mantra); from the *antaryāma*...

"By the fifteenfold [stoma], *ta=yā* (ibid. b, 7 with the *T* mantra); from the fifteenfold comes the *Bṛhat*, by that, *tayā=yā* (ibid. b, 8 with the *T* mantra); Bharadvāja is the seer of the *Bṛhat*; by that, *tayā=yā* (ibid. b, 9 with the *T* mantra), which has been grasped by Prajāpati, I grasp the mind for the sake of offspring; sit down, *ta=sīda* (ibid. b, 10 with the *T* mantra). Thus.

"To the north, the *suvar* [verse]" (4.3.2d,1). To the north: "By that deity" (T mantra), his hearing is *sauva*; "by that deity" (ibid. d,2 & T mantra), the autumn is *śrautra*; "by that" (ibid. d,3 & T mantra), the *anuṣṭubh* is *śāradī*; "by that" (ibid. d,4 & T mantra), from the *anuṣṭubh* comes the *svāra*; "by that" (ibid. d,5 & T mantra), from the *svāra* comes the *manthin*; "by that" (ibid. d,6 & T mantra), from the *manthin*...

"From the twenty-onefold [stoma], the Vairāja [sāman]; from the Vairāja, the seer Jamadagni; with thee taken by Prajāpati, I take the sense of hearing for the sake of offspring; by that divinity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. (4.3.2d, 1–10, with the respective *Taittirīya* mantras).

With the words, “This is the higher mind” (4.3.2e,1), he causes [the sacrificer] to recite while they are moving around on the right: “By that deity (T mantra); for her, speech is the mother; by that (ibid. f,2 with T mantra); may winter be for us through speech; by that (ibid. f,3 with T mantra); the *paṅkti* [meter] is for winter; by that (ibid. f,4 with T mantra); for the *paṅkti*, the *nidhanavat* [stotra]; by that (ibid. f,5 with T mantra); for the *nidhanavat*, the *āgrayaṇa* [graha]; by that (ibid. f,6 with T mantra)..."

The *āgrayaṇa* [cup] is associated with the *triṇava* and *trayastrimśa* [stomas]; by means of those two, the *śākvara* and *raivata* [sāmans]; by means of those two, Viśvakarman is the seer (*ṛṣi*). By you, who are grasped by Prajāpati, I grasp speech for the sake of progeny; by that, sit down—[thus, with the respective *T* mantras for each of 4.3.2f,1–10].

He causes fifty Apānabhṛt bricks to be laid down—ten in each of the directions. Ten people walk around them to the north of the Svayamātṛṇṇā brick; of those, they are laid down one by one, touching the Svayamātṛṇṇā diagonally.

He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *viṣūcī* bricks: "The eastern direction of the quarters" (TS 4.3.3a.1); he places one in the east. [He recites: "By that deity, of the seasons, the spring; by that [deity], Agni is the deity; by that [deity], the Brahman is the wealth; by that [deity], the *trivṛt* is the *stoma*; by that [deity], it has fifteen paths; by that [deity], the three-year-old steer... (TS 4.3.3a.2–6).

"Vayas, with that [tayā=yā] (ibid. a,7 with the *T* mantra); Kṛtam ayāna, with that [tayā=yā] (ibid. a,8 with the *T* mantra); Purovāto vāta, with that [tayā=yā] (ibid. a,9 with the *T* mantra); Sānaga Ṛṣi, with that [tayā=sīda] (ibid. a,10 with the *T* mantra)" (4.3.3a,1–10 with the *T* mantra for each)—thus he covers them with the verse beginning "O fathers, grandfathers" (4.3.3f,1): "The later and the earlier, may they protect us through the invocation of the gods [te naḥ pāntu = devahūtyān] (ibid. f to the end); with that [tayā=sīdata] (4.3.3f with the *T* mantra)."

"The western direction" (4.3.3c,1)—behind it is that which is the rainy season (*varṣā*) among the seasons; that which is the Viśve Devās among the deities; that which is wealth (*draviṇa*); that which is the seventeen-fold hymn-form (*stoma*); that which is the twenty-one-fold path; that which is the three-year-old steer (*trivatsa*) among the ages, the Dvāpara among the throws of the dice.

"Ta-yā (4.3.3c, 7 and 8 with the *T* mantra; note: the combination of c, 7–8 here is likely a scribe’s error)," "paścād vātō vātasa, ta-yā (4.3.3c, 9 with the *T* mantra)," "[K4, 58b11] ahabhūna ṛṣis, tayā sīda (4.3.3c, 10 with the *T* mantra)"—thus [the sequence from 4.3.3c, 1–10 with the *T* mantra for each;
as noted above, the scribe erred in joining c, 7 and c, 8 as if they formed a single mantra].

"O fathers, grandfathers," he says thus as he addresses them; "the southern direction of the quarters," he says as he addresses them from the south: "Thou art the summer of the seasons, thou art Indra the deity, thou art the kṣatra the wealth, thou art the fifteenfold stoma, and thou art the seventeenfold path."
"By that [Tretā], the age of the sun; by that, the [Tretā] of the three fires; by that, the southern wind; by that, the eternal seer—sit down! (4.3.3b, 1–10, with the *T* mantra for each).

He addresses them thus: "The fathers, the grandfathers" (4.3.3f, 1?). From the north, [he addresses them] with: "The northern direction" (4.3.3ḍ, 1). "She who belongs to the autumn among the seasons," "she who belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa as the deity," "she who belongs to nourishing wealth," "she who belongs to the twenty-one-fold hymn-form (*stoma*)," "she who belongs to the three-ninety-fold path. (4.3.3ḍ, 2–6 with the *T* mantras).

"Turyavāḍ vayas, with that [mantra]; āskando 'yānān, with that [mantra]; uttarādvāto vātas, with that [mantra]; pratna ṛṣis, with that—sit down [with the mantra]" (4.3.3d, 1–10, each with its respective *T* mantra).

He addresses them with the words, “The fathers, the grandfathers” (4.3.3f,1?). To the north, he makes him recite, “The upward direction of the quarters” (4.3.3e,1), while they are moving away. With the formula, “By that deity, Hemanta and Śiśira, the two seasons of the year; by that [deity], Bṛhaspati is the deity,” [K1,K4,.59a1] . . .

"Thou art the one who moves among the Trayastrimśa gods; by that deity, sit thou firm in the manner of Aṅgiras (with the respective *Tat* mantras). Thou art the age of the four-year-old ox; by that deity... Thou art the overcomer of those who do not come; by that deity... Thou art the wind blowing in all directions; by that deity... Thou art the seer Suparṇa; by that deity, sit thou firm in the manner of Aṅgiras."—thus [he addresses them], and [he addresses them] with "O fathers, O grandfathers" (4.3.3f,1?).

He consents: "The higher and the lower through the invocation of the gods... [K1,59a2] "...the river of the young women, who flows toward the river... [ṚV] ...of the young women... [K4,59a2] "...invoked by the gods."

"You seek a husband for your inviolable cows, O *aghnyā*s; by that deity, those [cows] of his yield the *sūdadohas* [milk]" (*ṚV* 8.69.2). Having placed one brick with the words "those very [cows] mix the *śoma*; by that [deity], sit down" (the *Sūtra* mantra to the end, together with the *Taittirīya* mantra), he should recite over it: "By that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm" (*Taittirīya* mantra). With two bricks: "By that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm. With many bricks: "By that deity, like Aṅgiras, sit firm."
[The Adhvaryu] causes [the bricks] to be brought forward. With another [formula], he lays down the *svayamātṛṇṇā* at the joint of the tail.

He makes [the sacrificer] recite the *haṃsapātinī* verses toward the north: "O *dharaṇasik*, by that deity; O *draviṇan*, by that [deity]; O *prasava*, by that [deity]; O *upayāma*, by that [deity]; O *kāṭas*, by that [deity]; O *arṇavas*, by that [deity]; O *sindhus*, by that [deity]; O *samudran*, by that [deity]; O *sarasvān*, by that deity; O *viśvavyacās*, by that [deity]; O *subhūtan*, by that [deity]; ... by that [deity], sit down! (with the mantra as in the Taittirīya).

He extends the limbs of the fire-altar, placing one brick at each joint and one in the middle. He lays down a brick in the east with the formula: "By the eastern quarter I settle thee"—(5.5.8.2–3[1]–1)—and with: "With the Gāyatrī metre, with Agni, I lay down the head; by that [brick] sit thou"—(5.5.8.2–3[1], to the end, with the *T* mantra).

To the south, he says: "By the southern quarter I settle thee"—(ibid. [2]–1)—and: "With the Triṣṭubh metre, with Indra, I lay down the wing; by that [brick] sit thou"—(ibid. [2], to the end, with the *T* mantra).

With the words, "I settle you in the western direction" (ibid. [3]-1), he places [the brick] in the west; with the words, "By means of the Jagatī metre, by Savitṛ, I place the tail; by that, sit down" (ibid.

[3] to the end, with the *T* mantra), and with the words, "I settle you in the northern direction" (ibid. [4]-1), he places it in the north; with the words, "By means of the Anuṣṭubh metre, for Mitra and Varuṇa, I place the wing; by that, sit down" (ibid. [4] to the end, with the *T* mantra).

"By the upward direction I settle thee"—thus in the middle; [with the mantra: "With the *pāṅkta* metre, with Bṛhaspati as the deity, with the back of Agni I place the back of Agni; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras"—thus (from ibid. [5] to the end, with the T-mantra).

To the south, behind the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick, he lays down the *prājāpatyā* brick and the *ṛṣabha* brick with the formula: "The image of the year" (TS 5.7.2b,1). With the *prājāpatyā* formula, "That which has pervaded thee... with that sit thou" (ibid., b to the end, with the *T* mantra), and with the *ṛṣabha* formula, "Thee, O Agni, the bull, the wise one... (TS 5.7.2a,1), he places the *ṛṣabha* brick upon it with the formula, "The youth again... sharpen him; with that sit thou" (ibid.).

At the end, with the *T* mantra—thus he extends the *sāmaciti* on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s; three in each of the directions and three in the middle. Of these, one touches each *svayamātṛṇṇā* among those facing together, and makes him recite: "O Agni, come for the feast" (*agna āyāhi vītaye*).
He places the *gāyatra* brick in the east with the formulas: “Being praised upon the sacrificial grass... with that deity, sit down” (TB 3.5.2.1–2; cf. ṚV 6.16.11–12).

With the verse, “We praise thee, O Hero” (*abhi tvā śūra nonuma*), he places the *rathantara* on the south; [and with] “Like milch-cows standing still...,” “O Indra, Lord of those who stand still...,” “Which has not been born...,” “Which has been born... we invoke,” and “Sit down with that one” (*tayāsīda*)—[thus, according to the *ApŚS* 17.8.4].

With the verse, "For we invoke thee indeed... (KS ibid. 129.14–15, 1; MS ibid. 158.18–159.1, 1), he performs the *bṛhat* on the northern wing to provide strength. [He recites: "Of the swift steed... (*śātā arvatas*, KS ibid., with the *Taittirīya* mantra), "...thee, O wielder of the stone... (*tvāṃ kāṣṭhā adrivas*, KS ibid. 16–17; MS ibid. 159.1–2, with the *Taittirīya* mantra), "...great is thy power for victory... (*mahas tavāno jigyuṣe*, KS ibid. 18–19, with the *Taittirīya* mantra)—thus [he says]. "Sit thou down... (*tayāsīda*).

"Yajñā-yajñā vo agnaye... (*KS ibid. 128.4–5, 1; MS ibid. 159.4–5, 1; TS 4.2.11 i, 1)" and "Kayā naś citra ābhuvat... (*KS ibid. 128.5–6; MS ibid. 159.6–7, with a T-mantra)... abhi su nas sakhīnām syūtibhis... sīda" (*KS ibid. 128.8–9; MS ibid. 159.8–9, with a T-mantra)—these constitute the Vāmadevya [Sāman] in the middle, [beginning] with "ūtī śaciṣṭhayā vṛtā" (at the end of the same passage).

"Yajñāyajñā vo agnayaḥ"—with these words [the *yajñāyajñīya* chant is performed] at the rear. "With song after song you grant skill; we shall praise the immortal Jātavedas, like a dear friend. (End of the passage). With that deity, "like a dear friend I have praised," [and] "O Son of Strength, for he is indeed devoted to us; let us serve him. (KS 39.12:130.1, refrain of the final verse).

"For the offering of the oblation" (KS ibid. 130.2; MS ibid. 159.12); "with that deity" (T mantra?); "may we serve with the offering of the oblation" (KS ibid., refrain); "be a helper in the contests for booty, be a prosperer, and a protector of our bodies" (KS ibid. 130.3; MS ibid. 159.13); "with that... sit down" (KS 39.12: 129.20–21, 130.1–2, 130.2–3, with the T-mantra for each; cf. MS 2.13: 159.10–13). Thus [it is said].
With the verse, "By what means has the wondrous one appeared for us? (*kayā naś citra ābhuvat*), he places the *vāmadevya* melody in the middle.

To the north, behind the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, he deposits the forms of the *ṛc* and the *sāman*: the form of the *sāman* is "by what means has the wondrous one appeared for us? (*kayā naś citra ābhuvat*), and the form of the *ṛc* is "with that aid, O Father, sit down" (*ūtī tāta tan tvābhis tayāsīda*). Thus, "with that aid, O Father, sit down" (*ūtī vṛtā, tayāsīda*) constitutes the form of the *ṛc*. (See *Taittirīya Saṃhitā* 4.2.11i; *Kāṭhaka Saṃhitā* 39.12:128.4–5).

With the verse, "All have magnified Indra" (4.6.3m, 1), he places the ocean-lord; with "Sit down with that" (4.6.3m, with the *T* mantra)—in this very manner these two are placed in the layers (*citī*) by way of successive turns.

There are nine space-filling bricks (*lokaṃpṛṇā*); he extends nine space-filling bricks toward the northern hip, up to the naturally perforated brick (*svayamātṛṇṇā*), while making him recite over them as they are arranged together.
"Fill the world"—with these words he lays down the first of them; "fill the gap, and then sit..."

*asīṣadan* (from the same source, at the end), with that deity (the mantra); *tā asya sūdadohasaḥ* (the mantra, 4.2.4o); with that deity (the mantra?); *nadaṃ vo adatīnām* (*ṚV* 8.69.2; *SV* 2.862; *Ā* 5.1.6; *ZZ*, *LZ*; in *ṚV* it is *nadaṃ va odatīnāṃ nadaṃ... iṣudhyasi*); with that deity; *tā asya sūdadohasaḥ*; *nadaṃ vo adatīnām* (*ṚV* 8.69.2); "fill the space"; *nadaṃ vo adatīnām* (*ṚV* 8.69.2).

With the verse, “Fill the world; may they yield for him” (*lokaṃ pṛṇa tā asya sūdadohasaḥ*), he places the tenth pan on the north side of the other pan, with the formula, “Fill the fissure; you have sat down; sit with her.

He has proceeded according to the *Ṛgveda* verse beginning with “The flowing one for you who do not flow” (*ṛdavatyā*). With the mantra, “You seek the flowing one for those who do not flow; with that deity, may they yield for him,” he addresses that very same pan.
They mix the *soma* in the luminous realm of heaven (*śomaṃ śrīṇanti rocane divaḥ*)— [reciting the mantra to its conclusion]—
"with that, sit down"— thus they cover the layer (*citiṃ*), saying, "Make it well-provided with bricks."

They pile up the edge-bricks; they make the appearance of the bricks excellent. Taking a branch of *udumbara* wood, the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer follow after the fire with the *lokaṃpṛṇā* and the *sūdadohas* formulas: "Fill the space, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are auspicious! May Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati establish you in this womb. (Var. 4.2.4n).

With the [mantras] "By that deity," "Those [cups] of his, yielding milk," and "By that deity, sit firm like the Aṅgirases" (the mantras from *tā asya sūdadohasaḥ* to the end of the *abhyākāra*), he begins from the right side with the [bricks] belonging to the head, then the right wing, then the tail, then the left wing; having completed them on the north side, he places the branch on the rubbish-heap (*utkara*).

Having deposited [the bricks] with the verse, "Come for our enjoyment" (*āyāhi vītaye*), and having laid down the layer (*citi*), he joins it together with the mantra, "Being praised upon the sacrificial grass... sit there with that" (from the same source, with the *t*-mantra). Then, with the mantra, "The conscious and the unconscious... sit there with that" (from the same source, with the *t*-mantra), he touches the layer-construction with the formula, "He who builds the layer... (5.5.4.4.1). Finally, he says, "May he build... sit there with that" (from the same source, with the *t*-mantra).

With the *gāyatrī* verse, "Agni is the head" (4.4.4a,1), he touches [the vessel]; then, having offered the oblation of the Daśahotṛ with the mantra, "The peak of heaven—he quickens; sit down with that" (ibid., end), he descends with the descent formula: "Giver of out-breath, giver of in-breath" (4.6.1q,1); "Giver of diffused breath—be auspicious" (ibid., end); "Homage to thee—be auspicious" (4.6.1m?); "May speech be in my mouth—do not harm me; do not abandon me" (4.6.1q, TA 10.72?).

Having descended with the mantra, "The fair-winged one, having taken refuge in the worlds," he worships the altar-pile (*citi*) with the mantra, "The falcon, winged, unaging, golden, the heron— may the *gāyatrī* protect the bull, the heavenly light, as he flies.
Having performed the *pravargya* and *upasads*, they dwell by the great altar-pile.

In the morning, having released his speech with the Āditya formula, he proceeds with the Pravargya and Upasad rites. He fastens the fire within himself and ascends by means of the *adhirohaṇa* (climbing-verse). Then, with the verse, "He who is questioned in heaven" (*pṛṣṭo divi*), he places a layer of loose earth (*purīṣa*). With the mantra, "By that [brick], sit down," he touches it with the formula, "The conscious and the unconscious. With the mantra, "By that, sit down," he [concludes].
He descends by means of the descent. Having performed the Pravargya and Upasad rites, they stay overnight;
in the morning, having released speech with the Āditya cup, he mounts the fire within himself.
Then, with the verse, "O Agni, from the ocean," he offers an oblation of loose earth (*purīṣa*): "That arrow of yours—may we become that; svāhā! (TS 5.5.9.1).
With the verse, "That I entreat of thee," he offers the *anucara* offering and descends by way of descent.
He proceeds with the Pravargya and Upasad rites; he mounts the fire within himself.

Then he arranges these bricks upon the altar: the Hotṛ and the Vibhakti; two seasonal bricks; eight Avakās; two Saṃyānīs; two Sayuj bricks; nine head-bricks; five Aśvinī bricks; five seasonal bricks; five Prāṇabhṛt bricks; five Vṛṣṭisani bricks; nineteen Vayasī bricks; twenty-one Indra-tanūs; twelve final Yonis; the limbs of Agni belonging to Prajāpati; the Carṣabha brick; the Sāmaciti; the Utsāma and Ayomukhi bricks; and nine Lokampṛṇā bricks.
And there is the *lokaṃpṛṇā*, many [bricks], the *sandhi*, the *abhīmarśa*, the *triṣṭubh*, the oblation of the Hotṛ, the descent, and the attendance;
this constitutes his duty after having laid down the Caturhotṛ—[he recites] the case-ending "Agnim" (5.5.6.1b) and [the formula] "Śukraś ca Śuciś ca" (4.4.11b, 1).

To the east, touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick, he places the two seasonal bricks (*ṛtavye*) with the mantra: “The two summer seasons, entering into the interior of Agni, the earth—the two summer seasons, being well-disposed, let them enter; by that [brick], sit ye both firmly” (4.4.11g, with the *tayā* mantra).

He then places an *avakā* plant upon them with the mantra: “Those moist wombs of thine, O Agni... those which are nest-like... sit here for the body; by that [brick], sit” (cf. TA 4.18, with the *tayā* mantra).

To the east, he lays down those eight *saṃyānī* bricks with the two *sayuj* formulas: “With the two joined ones, I join thee for the two *āghāra* libations; by that deity, with brilliance, I join thee with the two joined ones; by that [deity], sit thou” (4.4.5a2, a3)—repeating this mantra for each—with the *mūrdhanvatī* formula at the time of the head, he lays down nine bricks belonging to the head:
the *Aśvinī* (5), the *Ṛtavyā* (5), the *Prāṇabhṛt* (5), the *Vṛṣṭisanī* (5), the *Haṃsapātinī* (4—also called *Mūrdhanvatī* in BSS 10.38), and the *Vayasvatī* (15).

He lays down five *aśvinī* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*: one in each of the cardinal directions and one in the center. These remain close together, as it were, without touching one another. He places one in the east with the mantra, "Firmly established... (TS 4.3.4a,1), followed by "In this thy firm womb... sit thou here" (ibid., with the *t*-mantra). He places one in the south with "O skillful one... (TS 4.3.4b,1), followed by "Sit thou here, O father of skill... sit thou here" (ibid., with the *t*-mantra).
With the mantra "kulāyinī" (4.3.4c,1), he places it in the west; with "vasumatī iha tvā, tayā sīda" (ibid., end)—this being the *t* mantra—he places it in the west;
with "agneḥ purīṣam asi" (4.3.4d,1), he places it in the north; with "devayānī iha tvā, tayā sīda" (ibid., end)—this being the *t* mantra—he places it in the north;
with "divo mūrdhāsi" (4.3.4e,1), he places it in the middle; and with "pṛthivyā nābhir iha tvā, tayā sīda" (ibid., end)—this being the *t* mantra—he places it in the middle.

He brings forward five seasonal bricks (*ṛtavyā*) around the *svayamātṛṇṇā* (self-perforated brick): one in each of the directions and one in the middle. These are placed close together, yet they remain without touching.

He places them in the east with the formula: "In harmony with the seasons" (TS 4.3.4.1), followed by: "With the ordinances in harmony, with the ordinances in harmony; with the Vasus in harmony, with the gods who provide a dwelling for thee in harmony. For Agni Vaiśvānara, may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryus, settle thee here; sit thou here with that [brick]" (as per the mantra at the end of the same section).
With the mantra, "In harmony with the seasons," he places it to the south; with "In harmony with the Rudras, in harmony with the gods, sit upon your birthplace"— [with this mantra]—
and to the west with "In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ordinances, in harmony with the Ādityas, in harmony with the gods, sit upon your birthplace"— [with this mantra].
"To the north, with the mantra: *śajūr ṛtubhiḥ* (4.3.4f4,1), and *śajūr viśvair devaiḥ sajūr devair vayonādhai sīda* (ibid., to the end);
in the middle, with *śajūr ṛtubhiḥ* (4.3.4f5,1), and *śajūr vidhābhiḥ sajūr devaiḥ sajūr devair vayonādhai m iha tvā tayā deva sīda* (ibid., to the end). [K4,60a2]
He lays down five life-sustaining bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* so that they are each mutually touching.

He places one in the east with the mantra, “Protect my out-breath” (4.3.4g1), saying “Sit down with her”; he places one in the south with the mantra, “Protect my in-breath” (4.3.4g2), saying “Sit down with her.”
With the mantra "Protect my vyāna" (4.3.4g3), he places it behind; with the mantra "Sit thereon," [he does so];
with the mantra "My eye shines far and wide," he places it to the north; with the mantra "Sit thereon," [he does so];
with the mantra "Make my hearing resonant" (4.3.4g5), he places it in the middle; with the mantra "Sit thereon," [he does so].

He causes five rain-bringers to extend around the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick; they are each separately prepared. He places one in the east with the mantra, "Make the waters swell" (4.3.4h,1), followed by "Sit thereon";
in the south with "Quicken the plants" (4.3.4h,2), followed by "Sit thereon."
With the mantra "tayā sīda," he places it from behind with the words "dvipāt pāhi" (4.3.4h3);
from the north with the words "catuṣpād ava" (4.3.4h4); and in the middle with the words "divo vṛṣṭim eraya" (4.3.4h5). [K1, 60a4]

He causes the four companions to bring the *pū* bricks; he himself lays down the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks; and in the northern directions, he causes them to recite: "Vayus is the support, the overlord is the metre; by that [metre] sit thou! Kṣatra is the Vayu, the Mayanda is the metre; by that [metre] sit thou! Viśvakarman is the Vayu, the Parameṣṭhin is the metre; by that [metre] sit thou! Mūrdhan is the Vayu, Prajāpati is the metre; by that [metre] sit thou! (4.3.5.1[16]–[19], with the *t-mantra* added to each).
He stretches five fathoms on the southern hip and five on the northern; he causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stones while they are being laid down in a continuous line.

With the words, “Tryavir vayaḥ” (4.3.5.1[1]), he places [the brick] on the south side: “Thou art the Triṣṭubh metre; with thee, [be seated]. (End of the mantra). “Ādityavāḍ vayaḥ, Virāṭ metre; with thee, [be seated]. “Pañcāvīr vayaḥ, Gāyatrī metre; with thee, [be seated]. “Trivatsaḥ vayaḥ, Uṣṇihā metre; with thee, [be seated]. (4.3.5.1[4], with the *t*-mantra). “Turyavāḍ vayaḥ, Anuṣṭubh metre; with thee, sit down. (4.3.5.1[5], with the *t*-mantra).
"Mantra"—[with the respective *mantra* for each]—thus [ends the section]. (Note: 4.3.5.1[1][4][5]{[2][3][4]} are omitted here.)

To the north, [he recites]: "The draft-ox is the age; the *bṛhatī* is the metre; by that [metre]... (with the respective mantra); "The bull is the age; the *sato-bṛhatī* is the metre; by that [metre]... (with the respective mantra); "The steer is the age; the *kakubh* is the metre; by that [metre]... (with the respective mantra); "The milch-cow is the age; the *jagatī* is the metre; by that [metre]... (with the respective mantra); "The ox is the age; the *paṅkti* is the metre... (with the respective mantra).

With the mantra, "By that [brick] sit down" (4.3.5.1[10]), and with the mantra for each, "The goat is our vigor" (4.3.5.1[11], 1), he places [the brick] on the right shoulder; with the mantra, "The *vivalat* metre, by that sit down" (ibid., to the end), and with the mantra, "The bull is our vigor" (4.3.5.1[12], 1), he places [the brick] on the left shoulder; with the mantra, "The *viśāla* metre, by that sit down" (ibid., to the end).

With the formula, "The tiger is the strength" (4.3.5.1[14]), he places [a brick] on the southern wing, saying, "The unassailable is the metre; sit upon it" (ibid., with the *t* mantra). With "The lion is the strength" (4.3.5.1[15]), he places one on the northern wing, saying, "The covering is the metre; sit upon it" (ibid., with the *t* mantra).
With "The man is the strength" (4.3.5.1[13]), he places one in the middle, saying, "The wearying is the metre; sit upon it" (ibid., with the *t* mantra).

He spreads out twenty-one *indratanū* bricks around the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick—five in each of the four directions and one in the middle. Of these, each one is touching a *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick. While they are aligned, he makes him recite.

With the formula, "By Agni, the All-conquering" (4.4.8.1), he places [the bricks] in front; [with the formulas: "By that [brick], the Self-ruler through Sūrya" (ibid. 2, with the *tayā* mantra); "By that [brick], the Lord of Power through Kratu" (ibid. 3, with the *tayā* mantra); "By that [brick], Tvaṣṭṛ through the Bull" (ibid. 4, with the *tayā* mantra); "By that [brick], Maghavan through the Sacrifice—sit down! (ibid. 5, with the *tayā* mantra). Each of these is accompanied by its respective *tayā* mantra.

"By the sacrificial fee, [he attained] heaven" (ibid. [6]); thus [he says] toward the south: "By that deity, sit! By wrath, the slayer of Vṛtra; by that, sit! By benevolence, the bestower of bodies; by that, sit! By food, the master of the household; by that, sit! By the earth, he established [the world]; by that, sit! (ibid. [6]–[10], with the *tat* mantra for each).

"With the *ṛc*s, the eater of food" (ibid. [11]), [he says] at the back; "with that deity, prospering through the *vaṣaṭ*-call, sit thou [there] with her" (ibid. [12], with the *t* mantra); "with the *sāman*, the protector of the body, sit thou [there] with her" (ibid. [13], with the *t* mantra); "with the *virāj*, possessing light, sit thou [there] with her" (ibid. [14], with the *t* mantra); "with the *brahman*, the drinker of soma, sit thou [there] with her" (ibid. [15], with the *t* mantra) (4.4.8.1[11]–[15]).

"By means of the cows, he established the sacrifices" (ibid. [16])—thus to the north: "By that deity, by the kṣatra, [he established] men; by that (ibid. [17], with the *tat* mantra), by means of the horse and the chariot, [he became] the wielder of the thunderbolt; by that (ibid. [18], with the *tat* mantra), by means of the seasons, [he became] the lord; by that (ibid. [19], with the *tat* mantra), by means of the year, [he became] the encompasser; by that—sit down (ibid. [20], with the *tat* mantra)" (4.4.8.1 [16]–[20]).

"Unassailable through austerity, being the sun with his bodies, having attained preeminence through truth"—with these three [verses], he places one brick in the middle. With the mantra "Sit down with that," he places twelve womb-bricks, the limbs of Agni, the one belonging to Prajāpati, the bull, the *sāmaciti*, the forms of the *ṛc* and *sāman*, nine *lokaṃpṛṇā*s, and one *lokaṃpṛṇā* and many others.

He says, “Cover the *citi*,” and having placed the final brick with the formula “Those [waters] of his, yielding good milk” (*tā asya sūdadohasaḥ*), he inserts [the formula] “We choose the messenger” (*dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe*; cf. 5.5.6.1b). Having laid down the *citi*, he joins it together with the formula “The Hotṛ of good wisdom... sit there with that” (*hotāraṃ sukṛtuṃ tayā sīda*; cf. ibid., 5.5.6b, 2.5.8.5, TB 3.5.2.3[1]).
He touches it with the formula “The conscious, the unconscious” (*citiṃ acitiṃ*; 5.5.4.4,1) and [concludes] with the mantra “Sit there with that” (*tayā sīda*).

With the *triṣṭubh* verse, "Bhuva" (4.4.4d,1), he touches [the altar]; having offered the oblation of the Caturhotṛ with the formula, "O bearer of the sacrifice's oblations, sit down with that" (ibid., at the end, with the *mantra*), he descends with the words, "Giver of breath, giver of out-breath (4.6.1q [prat]), obeisance to your heat and flame (ibid., 1 [prat]), may speech be in my mouth (5.5.9.2g; #TA10.72?), I implore you... (6) the eagle, resting upon the worlds, [attains] heaven" (?), and then stands worshipping the *citi*. With the formula, "The falcon, winged, [attains] the heavenly world" (?).
Having performed the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites, they stay overnight for the sake of the second layer (*city*).
In the morning, having released their speech with the *āditya* formula, they perform the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites; having performed them, they stay overnight.
In the morning, [he offers] to the Sun... indeed... he offers an oblation of loose soil (purīṣa) with the mantra: "That arrow of yours—may we become it, svāhā! (TS 5.5.9.1e).
With the verse "I entreat you," he arranges the accompanying [verse].

The *hotṛ*, the *vibhakti*, the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, the *hiraṇyeṣṭakā*, the *maṇḍaleṣṭakā*, the *samrāj*, the *retassic*, the *viśvajyotis*, four *ṛtavyā*s, two *avakā*s, eight *saṃyānī*s, one *sayuṅ*, nine [others], thirty-six *prāṇabhṛt*s, fourteen *bṛhatī*s, thirty-three *vālakhilyā*s, twelve *yajñatanū*s at the end, the *yonis* of Agni, the *aṅgas*, the *marśa*, and the *jagatī*: this is the *ho-kārya*.

Having laid down the *pañcahotṛ* brick, he pronounces the case-ending with the words “...by means of Agni. With the words “O Bhūvas, the life of all,” he takes up the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick; having grasped it with curd, he lays it down with the formula: “I lay you down together with them. Then the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer recite the *yajus*: “O Indra and Agni, [lay this] unshaking [brick],” and “With that which is most peaceful, sit thou there.”

Having placed this brick with the formula "Bhuvaḥ," he breathes over it. With the formula, "I have stepped upon the atmosphere, the best path" (5.6.8.1a2), he steps upon it with his two thumbs. With the formula, "May progeny not forsake me" (ibid., end), the Prastotṛ places a gold brick upon it while reciting, "Consciousness is the light; you are light" (5.7.6c2,1). He says, "Bestow light upon me; bestow the atmosphere; protect me from the atmosphere; sit down with her" (ibid., end, with the *t*-mantra).

With the verse, "The heaven and the mid-region have been entered by the *brahman*" (4.4.5d, 1), he places the *maṇḍala* brick, touching it with the western *svayamātṛṇṇā*, with the mantra: "The Maruts be your guardians, and Vāyu your armor; sit down with her" (ibid., end).
With the verse, "The Sovereign (*samrāj*) has established the light" (4.2.9p2), he places the *samrāj* brick, touching it with the eastern *svayamātṛṇṇā*, with the mantra: "Sit down with her."

With the formula, "Thou art the sovereign, the shedder of seed," he places the *retassic* brick to its south. With the formula, "Mayst thou conquer the intermediate space through her; sit down with her," [he places it].
With the formula, "May Viśvakarman settle thee," he places the *viśvajyotis* brick to its east. [He recites: "Of the intermediate space, Vāyu is thy overlord; sit down with her."

With the formula, "ṅabhaś ca nabhasyaś ca" (ŚB 4.4.11c,1), he places the two seasonal bricks (*ṛtavye*)—which are not touched by the *svayamātṛṇṇā*—with the mantra: "The two rainy seasons; O two seasonal bricks, sit firm upon the end of Agni, facing the rainy seasons" (ŚB 4.4.11c, *ibid.* g, with the *ṛk* mantra).
He then places the *avakā* plant over them with the mantra: "O Agni, those moist wombs of yours... (*TA* 4.18.1?), ending with: "...those which are firm, sit down" (*ibid.*, with the *ṛk* mantra).

With the formula, "Iṣa and Ūrja" (4.4.11d), he places those two *ṛtavyā* bricks using the preceding [mantra]; and with "The two autumnal seasons, O Agni... Heaven and Earth, the two autumnal seasons... sit down" (ibid., end; ibid. f, with a *t*-mantra); and with "Those which are yours, O Agni, moist... (#TA 4.18.1?)—he extends those eight *saṃyānī* bricks using the preceding [mantra], and one *sayuj* brick with "I yoke you with splendor, with the yoke-fellow; with her, sit down" (4.4.5a4, with a *t*-mantra). (For the analysis of 4.4.5a, see BSS Tr. p. 543, n. 79.)
At the time for the head, he lays down nine bricks pertaining to the head:
the *diśyās*, the *prāṇabhṛts*, the *bṛhatīs*, and the *vālakhilyās*.

He causes five *diśyā* bricks to be brought forward on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*; one in each of the directions and one in the middle. These remain close together, as it were, without touching one another.
He lays down the first one in the east with the formula: "Thou art the queen, the eastern direction. With the mantra "sit down by means of her," he places them.
"To the south, with the mantra: 'Thou art Virāj, the southern quarter; sit thou with her' (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.1.3);
to the west, with the mantra: 'Thou art Śamrāj, the western quarter; sit thou with her'; to the north, with the mantra: 'Thou art Svarāj, the northern quarter; sit thou with her.'"

With the words, "Thou art the sovereign, the great quarter" (ibid. c5), he places [the brick] in the middle; with the mantra "Sit down by means of her," he lays down the ten *prāṇabhṛt* bricks to the east of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*; he causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *haṃsapātinī* bricks in the northern directions.

"Protect my life-span, by that deity; protect my out-breath, by that deity; protect my in-breath, by that deity; protect my diffused breath, by that deity; protect my eye, by that deity; protect my ear, by that deity; quicken my mind, by that deity; nourish my speech, by that deity; protect my self, by that deity; grant me light, by that deity."

With the formula "tayā sīda" (TS 4.3.6d1–10), he lays down thirty-six *bṛhatī* bricks—twelve to the south, twelve to the west, and twelve to the north. He causes the sacrificer to recite over them as they are being laid down in a continuous line, each one touching a *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone.

With the words, “*mā chandas*,” he places [the brick] on the south; with “*tayā devatayā, pramā chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, pratimā chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, astrīvic chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, paṅktiś chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, uṣṇihā chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, bṛhatī chandas*,” with “*tayā devatayā, anuṣṭup chandas*,” and with “*tayā devatayā, virāṭ chandas*.”

"By that which has the *gāyatrī* metre (4.3.7a10), by that which has the *triṣṭubh* metre (4.3.7a11), by that which has the *jagatī* metre (4.3.7a12)—sit! (4.3.7a1–a12, with a *t* mantra for each). Following this, [he recites] "The earth is the metre" (4.3.7a13), and then: "By that which has the *antarikṣa* as its metre (4.3.7a14), by that which has the sky as its metre (4.3.7a15), by that which has the seasons as its metre (4.3.7a16), by that which has the constellations..."

"By *chandas* (meter) [which is she], by *manaś-chandas* (the meter of mind) [which is she], by *vāk-chandas* (the meter of speech) [which is she], by *kṛṣiś-chandas* (the meter of agriculture) [which is she], by *hiraṇyaṃ-chandas* (the meter of gold) [which is she], by *gauś-chandas* (the meter of the cow) [which is she], by *ajā-chandas* (the meter of the goat) [which is she], by *aśvaś-chandas* (the meter of the horse) [which is she]—sit down with her! (4.3.7a13–a24, with a separate *t*-mantra for each).

"Agni is the deity" (4.3.7a25)—thus [he says] to the north: "By that [power], Vāta is the deity" (ibid. a26); "by that [power], Sūrya is the deity" (ibid. a27); "by that [power], Candramas is the deity" (ibid. a28); "by that [power], the Vasus are the deities" (ibid. a29); "by that [power], Rudra is the deity" (ibid. a30); "by that [power], the Ādityas are the deities" (ibid. a31); "by that [power], the Viśve Devāḥ are the deities" (ibid. a32); "by that [power], the Maruts are the deities" (ibid. a33); "by that [power], Bṛhaspati... [K4, 60b13] ...is the deity."

"By that which has the deity Indra (ibid. a35), by that which has the deity Varuṇa (ibid. a36)—sit! (4.3.7a25–a36, with a *t*-mantra for each). Thus he lays down fourteen *vālakhilyā* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*: seven in front and seven behind. Each one of these is laid down touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* diagonally.
While they are being laid out in various directions, he causes [the sacrificer] to recite: "Thou art the head, the sovereign" (4.3.7b1).

In front, the Adhvaryu lays down [the bricks] with the formula: "By that deity, you are firm, a support; by that [deity], you are a restrainer, a restrainer; for food, you; by that; for strength, you; by that; for agriculture, you; by that; for security, you; by that, sit" (4.3.7b1–b7).

"O controller, O sovereign! (ibid. b8)—thus the Pratiprasthātṛ [recites] afterwards: "By that deity—[thou art] *dhruvā* (fixed), *dharaṇī* (supporting) (ibid. b9); by that—[thou art] *dhartrī* (sustainer), *dharitrī* (upholder) (ibid. b10); by that—for life (*āyuse*) thee (ibid. b11); by that—for splendor (*varcase*) thee (ibid. b12); by that—for vigor (*ojase*) thee (ibid. b13); by that deity—for strength (*balāya*) thee (ibid. b14); by that—sit down (*sīda*)" (4.3.7b8–b14).
This is the *Yajñatanū* (33) and the *Yoni* (12). [K1,61a2–; K4, 61a2–; M282-3]

{In Caland, fourth Maṇḍala, No. 112 (pp. 233–4), there is an Anvākhyāna concerning the Yajñatanū-iṣṭi, which is not found in the Sūtra.} He extends thirty-three sacrificial bodies: eight in each of the directions and one in the middle. Of these, each one touches a Svayamātṛṇṇā stone; he causes [the sacrificer] to recite over them as they are aligned.

"Prajāpati with the mind"—with these words he places [the bricks] in front. "With that deity, O Andhas-cchedas; with that, O Dhātṛ, at the consecration; with that, O Savitṛ, at the maintenance; with that, O Pūṣan, at the purchase of the Soma; with that, O Varuṇa, when bound; with that, O Asura, while being prepared; with that, O Mitra, when purchased—sit down with that. Thus [he says]. (4.4.9.1–8)

"O Śipiviṣṭa, thou art seated! (4.4.9.1.9)—thus [he says] to the south. "With her, O Narandhiṣa, being pushed forward! (ibid. 10); "With her, the Overlord has arrived! (ibid. 11); "With her, Prajāpati, being led forth! (ibid. 12); "With her, Agni, in the Āgnīdhra fire-shed! (ibid. 13); "With her, Bṛhaspati, being led forth from the Āgnīdhra! (ibid. 14); "With her, Indra, in the Havirdhāna shed! (ibid. 15); "With her, Aditi, thou art seated! (ibid. 16)—with these [mantras], he says for each: "Sit down with her! (4.4.9.1.9–16).

"Viṣṇu, being brought down"—thus [he says] from behind; then: "By that deity, O Atharvan, thou art poured out" (ibid. 18); "by that deity, O Yama, thou art pressed" (ibid. 19); "by that deity, O purifier of the unpurified, thou art shaken" (ibid. 20); "by that deity, O Vāyu, thou art being purified" (ibid. 21); "by that deity, O Mitra, thou art mixed with milk" (ibid. 22); "by that deity, O Manthin, thou art mixed with barley-meal" (ibid. 23); "by that deity, O Vaiśvadeva, thou art drawn up—sit down by that deity" (ibid. 24). For each [of these], there is a *t*-mantra.

"O Rudra, thou art invoked" (ibid. 25)—thus [he places it] to the north—"with that [power] by which Vāyu turned back" (ibid. 26), "by which Nṛcakṣas became visible" (ibid. 27), "by which the portion arrived" (ibid. 28), "by which the *nārāśaṃsa* of the fathers [was offered]" (ibid. 29), "by which the Asura was consumed" (ibid. 30), "by which the Sindhu went down to the purificatory bath (*avabhṛtha*)" (ibid. 31), "by which the ocean entered" (ibid. 32)—"with that [power], sit down" (4.4.9.25–32, with the *t* mantra for each).

With the two verses, "The waters have overflowed; the sun has reached its zenith" (ibid. 33–34), he places one brick in the middle. With the formula, "Sit down with that," he lays down the twelve *yoni* bricks.
Having placed the branch of the *agni* tree and recited, "The fire is kindled" (*agniḥ samidhyate*; *Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 5.5.6c, cf. 1.4.46l = 3.5.11s, #TB 2.7.12.3), he joins the layer.
For the abbreviation, cf. ī, lines 20–22 and lines 115–118. He concludes with the mantra: "The sage, the master of the house, whose mouth is the *juhū* ladle; sit down with that" (ibid., to the end).
He touches [the altar] with the words, "Consciousness and unconsciousness" (5.5.4.4,1), and with the mantra, "By that, sit down.
With the *jagatī* verse, "The guardian of the people has been born, the watchful one" (4.4.4g,1), he touches it, and with the mantra, "Agni, the very skillful and pure for the Bharatas...
by that, sit down" (ibid., end), having offered the oblation of the Pañcahotṛ, they proceed with the "giver of breath" and dwell at the middle layer of the altar.
In the morning, having released their speech with the sun, they perform the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites and dwell [therein].

In the morning, having released their speech with the sun, they place the fire within themselves and offer an oblation of soil with the verse, “O Agni, come hither... (RV 10.188.1). Then, with the formula, “Those who went forth... may we be many, svāhā! (cf. ŚB 12.4.1.35–36), he offers the oblation.
With the verse, “*Tat tvā yāmi*,” he offers the *anucārī* oblation and ascends.

Then he arranges these layers (*citi*). There are two to be performed: the *hotṛ* and the *vibhakti*. There are two *avakāṣṭha*s, two *saṃyānī*s, two *sayuj* bricks, nine *śīrṣaṇyā*s, the *anubrāhmaṇa*, the *akṣṇayāstomīya*s, the *sṛṣṭi*s, the *apyuṣṭi*s, twelve *aindraujasa*s, twelve final *yoni*s, the *abhīmarśa*, and the *anuṣṭubh*; this constitutes the duty of the *hotṛ*.

Having placed the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* [formula], he pronounces the case-ending "Agni" (4.3.13a, 1?; cf. 5.5.6.1d) and "sahaś ca sahasyaś ca" (4.4.11e, 1). He then places the two *ṛtavyā* bricks, touching them to the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick on the east, with the mantra: "O Agni, you two who belong to the winter season (*haimantika*), settle down firmly" (Tmantra; cf. 4.4.11e, with T-mantra).

With the formula, “Those of thine, O Agni, that are moist... sit down” (*TA* 4.18, with the *t*-mantra), he places those eight *saṃyānī* bricks with the preceding [formula]. With the two *sayuj* bricks using the formulas, “With hymns I yoke thee... (*4.4.5a4*), with that [brick] sit down,” and “With chants I yoke thee... (*ibid.* a5), with that [brick] sit down” (*4.4.5a4–a5*, with the *t*-mantra for each), he places nine *śīrṣaṇyā* bricks at the time of the head, according to the *Anubrāhmaṇa*. He extends the *akṣṇayāstomīya* bricks in a diagonal fashion, beginning with the *Haṃsapātinī*.
On all sides, he places seven *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks in each of the directions—namely, the *haṃsapātinī*s—in the east and the north.

He causes [the sacrificer] to recite, "The swift one, the threefold" (*TS* 4.3.8.1,1), as he lays them down in the east; with the mantra "Sit thereon," he places them in the south with "The vault, the seventeenfold" (*ibid.*, 3), saying "Sit thereon."
He places [the bricks] with the mantra "taḥ sīda" (sit there), [placing one] behind with "dharuṇa ekaviṃśaḥ" (the twenty-first is the support),

to the north with "bhāntaḥ pañcadaśaḥ" (the fifteen are radiant), and to the east with "pratūrtir aṣṭādaśaḥ" (the eighteen is the impulse). Each is accompanied by the mantra "tayā sīda" (sit with that).

With the mantra "The *abhivarta* is the twentyfold" (Ibid., 6), [he places it] to the south; with the mantra "Sit with that," [he places it] to the west with "The *varcas* is the twenty-twofold" (Ibid., 8);
and to the north with the mantra "Sitting with that," [he places it] with "Austerity is the nineteenfold" (Ibid., 5).
He places [the brick] in the east with the words, "The womb is the twenty-fourth" (Ibid., 10), and with "Sit thereon" (*tayā sīda*);
in the south with "The embryos are the twenty-fifth" (Ibid., 11), and with "Sit thereon"; in the west with "Vital force is the twenty-sevenfold" (Ibid., 12), and with "Sit thereon."
He places [the bricks] with the formula "tayā sīda" [to the north], saying "śambharaṇas trayoviṃśaḥ";
[with "tayā sīda"] to the east, saying "kratur eka ekatriṃśaḥ";
and [with "tayā sīda"] to the south, saying "bradhnasya viṣṭapaṃ catustriṃśaḥ."
[He places a brick] to the west with the formula, "The Trayastriṃśa is the foundation;
sit thereon"; to the north with "The Nāka is the thirty-sixfold;
sit thereon"; to the east with "Thou art the portion of Agni; sit thereon"; and [in the center] with "Dīkṣā is the Trivṛt Stoma; sit thereon."

"To the north of the *ṛṣabha* bricks, he places them with the formulas: "Thou art the portion of the far-seeing ones"—to the south; "The *dhātu* is the hymn-form (*stoma*), sit thou therewith"—to the west;

"Thou art the portion of Mitra"—to the north; and "Thou art the portion of Varuṇa, sit thou"—and "Thou art the portion of Indra, sit thou"—with the mantra "To Viṣṇu, sit thou."* *(Note: The bracketed portions indicate the reconstruction of the missing text based on the parallel structure of the ritual sequence.)*
He places [the bricks] in the east with the mantra, "Thou art the portion of the Vasus"; in the south with "Thou art the portion of the Rudras...
sit" (Ibid., f+t mantra); in the west with "Thou art the portion of the Ādityas" (?); and in the north with "Thou art the portion of Pūṣan... sit" (Ibid., e+t mantra).
He places [the bricks] on the north with the mantra, "Thou art the portion of the god Savitṛ" (TS 4.3.8.1); on the east with "Sit upon the impulse of Bṛhaspati" (Ibid.
and "The Dhartra is the Catuṣṭoma" (Ibid.); on the south with "Sit with her" (? cf.
4.3.8.1,18) and "Thou art the portion of the Yāvāns" (TS 4.3.9i + t mantra).

"Thou art the portion of the Ṛbhus"—thus [he places it] behind. "The Stoma of the Viśve Devas; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras"—thus [he places it] on the north, saying, "The Vivarta is the forty-eightfold [Stoma]; by that deity, sit firm" (ŚB 4.3.8.1,17 + respective mantras).
He extends the *sṛṣṭi* bricks all around the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s; four in each of the four directions and one in the middle. Of these, each [*sṛṣṛti* brick] touches one *svayamātṛṇṇā*.

Some lay them down according to the order of their creation, beginning with "They praised with one" (TS 4.3.10.1). He lays them down touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* in the east with the mantra: "The progeny was intent upon her; sit down with her" (ibid., with the mantra).
With seven [verses] they praised it—thus, before [the first], the Seven Seers sat upon the outermost [ring] with the mantra "Sit thou" (ibid., end);
with three [verses] they praised it—thus, within that, Brahmā sat upon the intermediate [ring] with the mantra "Sit thou" (ibid., end);
with five [verses] they praised it—thus, within that, the Beings sat upon the innermost [ring] with the mantra "Sit thou" (ibid., end).

With the mantra, "They praised with nine" (ibid. [5], 1), he places [a brick] touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* from the south; with the mantra, "O Fathers, sit down" (ibid., at the end), and with "They praised with fifteen" (ibid.
[8], 1), he places the final [brick] from the south; and with the mantra, "The kṣatra was created;
sit down" (ibid., at the end).

With the words, "They praised with eleven," (ibid. [6],1), he places [a brick] within that space with the mantra, "The seasons, sit down" (ibid., at the end); with the words, "They praised with thirteen," (ibid. [7],1), he places [a brick] within that space with the mantra, "The months, sit down" (ibid., at the end);
with the words, "They praised with seventeen," (ibid. [9],1), he subsequently places [a brick] touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* with the mantra, "The cattle, sit down" (ibid., at the end).

With twenty-three [verses] they praised—the last [verse] being "O low-born one, sit down" (with that mantra at the end); with nineteen [verses] they praised—the intermediate [verse] being "O Śūdra-Aryan, sit down" (with that mantra at the end);
with twenty-one [verses] they praised—the intermediate [verse] being "The one-hoofed animals, sit down" (with that mantra at the end).

With the words, “They praised with twenty-five” (ibid. [13], 1), he places [a brick] to the north, touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* [brick], with the mantra ending, “Wild animals were created... sit down” (ibid., to the end). With the words, “They praised with thirty-one” (ibid. [16], 1), he places the final [brick] to the north, with the mantra ending, “Creatures were created, and the *yava*s and *āyava*s...

sit down” (ibid., to the end). With the words, “They praised with twenty-seven” (ibid. [14]), he places [a brick] between those two, with the mantra ending, “Heaven and earth... sit down” (ibid., to the end).
With twenty-nine [verses] they praised—"thus it is said at the end of that [section]"—with the mantra "O trees, sit down";

with thirty-three [verses] they praised—"thus it is said in the middle"—"The beings were appeased; Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin was the overlord; by that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm. (End of section, with the mantra).
He extends the *vyuṣṭi*-bricks with the eastern [formula]. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite the *haṃsapātinī* bricks while they face northward;
some lay them down facing westward, saying, "The dawn indeed breaks toward the west. Others lay them down facing all directions, saying, "The dawn indeed breaks from every side."

He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over those facing west; he establishes them facing north with the formula: "This indeed is she whom the *mahiman* cups attend (4.3.11a); by that deity, the first wife of the seasons—everything else [is the same as before]—by that, sit down.

Thus he extends twelve bricks of Indra’s vigor on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s, three in each direction. Of these, each one touches a *svayamātṛṇṇā*. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over those facing together with the formula:
"For strength thee"—thus he places one in front—"by that [deity], for increasing strength thee"—thus [another]—"for upward strength thee, by that, sit down."

"To thee for great age"—thus on the south; "with that [which is] 'sā sahe tvā', with that [which is] 'ta=yā', with that which is 'sahīyase tvā', with that—sit!"—"to thee for the overcoming"—thus on the west; "with that [which is] 'tayā=yā', with that [which is] 'sā sahe tvāta=yā', with that which is 'abhīṣāce tvā', with that—sit!"—"to thee for the overpowering"—thus on the north; "with that [which is] 'ta=yā', with that which is 'abhimātiṣāce tvā', with that [which is] 'abhimati ji . . . sit!"—thus.
He lays down twelve womb-bricks with the verse, “O Agni, may he strike down his Vṛtra-like enemies.
Having laid down the layer (*citi*), he joins it together with the formula, “Desiring wealth, invoked—sit thou with that.
He touches it with the words, “The conscious and the unconscious,” and with the formula, “Sit thou with that. (5.5.4.4 + mantra).

With the *anuṣṭubh* verse, “O you of most wondrous fame” (4.4.4.3k), he touches it. [He recites: “They call upon you to carry [the oblation]... [and so on through the formulas of the] *ṣaḍḍhotṛ*... “O giver of out-breath, giver of in-breath, leading to heaven” (cf.
4.6.1.4–5q). Having performed the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites, they stay for the fourth layer (*cityā*).
In the morning, having released his speech with the Āditya [formula], he ascends by means of the Pravargya and Upasad rites;
then, with the words "O Agni, what is the stone? (ŚB 5.5.9.1), he offers an oblation of loose earth and ascends with the verse "That arrow of yours... (ŚB 5.5.9.1e).

Then he piles these bricks: the Hotṛ and the Vibhakti; two seasonal bricks; eight *avakā* plants; two *saṃyānī* bricks; two *sayuj* bricks; nine head-bricks (*śīrṣaṇyāḥ*); forty-five *asapatnā* bricks; forty *virāj* bricks; thirty-one *stomabhāga* bricks; five *nākasad* bricks; five *pañcacoḍā* bricks; twenty-eight *chandas* bricks; five *vṛṣṭisani* bricks; eight *ādityeṣṭakā* bricks; five *ghṛteṣṭakā* bricks; five *ya.e . . .(16)dās*; seven *ayudhā* bricks...
(4) There are five *ājyānīs*, four *rāṣṭrabhṛts*, twelve *bhūteṣṭakās*, three *vedarūpas*, and finally twelve *yonis*—the *sandhi* and the *abhīmarśa*; this constitutes his work.
Having laid down the *saptahotṛ*, he pronounces the case-ending of Agni:
"Tapaś ca tapasyaś ca" (4.4.11.1ff). ... (8) "The seasons... the two winter seasons (*śaiśira*)... the earth... the two winter seasons... [grant]... (cf. ibid. g).

With the verse, “Those which are thine, O Agni... sit down” (*yās te agne... sīda*), he places those eight *saṃyanī* bricks using the first [formula]. Two are joined together with the formula, “By the meters, by the deity, for the increase of wealth, for the preeminence among kinsmen, I join thee with me as thy companion; with that [companion]... sit down” (4.4.5a6, with the *t* mantra).
At the time of the head, he places nine head-bricks (*śīrṣaṇyā*). He causes five *asapatnā* bricks to extend [forward]. (40) [K1,62a3-b3; K4,62a3- ; M288-290]
The *purīṣavatī* (4), the *virāj* (40), the *stomabhāga* (31), the *patnī* (= *nākasad* in BSS) (5), and the *patnī* (= *pañcacoḍā* in BSS) (5). [Check M289, cf.
Akh <30>, p. 622–3, where they are called "pañcacodā"!].
One places each of these around the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, with the *purīṣavatī* in the center, as if in close proximity.
They remain untouched;

he places them in front with the mantra, “O Agni, those born [from thee],” and concludes with, “Drive away our rivals, sit down with that power. He places them behind with the mantra, “Those born by force,” and concludes with, “Drive away our enemies, sit down with that power.”
"To the south, with the formula: 'The four-and-forty-fold hymn-form (stoma), splendor (varcas) as wealth; sit thou here with that' (4.3.12c); to the north, with the formula:
