'The sixteen-fold hymn-form, vigor (ojas) as wealth; sit thou here with that' (ibid.); and in the middle, he places the *purīṣavatī* brick with the formula: 'Thou art the soil of the earth, named Apas; sit thou here with that' (4.3.12e). (Cf. *Asapatnās* of BSS 10.45:42.16ff; p. 567).

He spreads forty *virāj* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s, ten in each direction; one by one, they are laid touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s diagonally. Or, he makes him recite while they are being laid facing each other.

He places them in front with the formula: "May *chanda* grant space for us" (4.3.12.f1). "With that, may *chanda* grant us space" (*ibid*. f2); "with that, may *chanda* be auspicious for us" (*ibid*. f3); "with that, may *chanda* encompass us" (*ibid*. f4); "with that, may *chanda* reach us" (*ibid*. f5); "with that, may *chanda* be our mind" (*ibid*. f6); "with that, may *chanda* be our expanse" (*ibid*. f7); "with that, may *chanda* be the river" (*ibid*. f8); "with that, may *chanda* be the ocean" (*ibid*. f9); "with that, may *chanda* be the flood."
"Chandas (ibid. f10), tayā sīda" (4.3.12.f1–f10, with a *mantra* for each)—thus [it is said].

"Kakuc-chandas" (4.3.12.f21); thereafter: "tayā-yā, trikakuc-chandas" (ibid. f22), "tayā-yā, kāvyaṃ chandas" (ibid. f23), "ta-yā, aṅku-pañ chandas" (ibid. f24), "ta-yā, padapaṅktiś chandas" (ibid. f25), "ta-yā, akṣarapaṅktiś chandas" (ibid. f26), "ta-yā, viṣṭārapaṅktiś chandas" (ibid. f27), "ta-yā, kṣuro bhṛjvāñ chandas" (ibid. f28), "ta-yā, prachac chandas" (ibid. f29), "ta-yā."
"O winged meter, sit down by means of her"—thus [the ritual action is performed] with the *t*-mantra for each [meter] (4.3.12f.21–f.30).
(K4, 62a7; M289) [The photograph of M is quite unclear!]

"Śaṃyac-chandas," (ibid. f11)—thus on the south; "tayā-yā, viyac-chandas" (ibid. f12), "tayā, bṛhat-chandas" (ibid. f13), "tayā, rathantaram-chandas" (ibid. f14), "tayā, nikāyaś-chandas" (ibid. f15), "tayā, vivadhaś-chandas" (ibid. f16), "tayā, giraś-chandas" (ibid. f17?), "tayā, bhrajaś-chandas" (ibid. f18), "tayā, ṣaṣṭup-chandas" (ibid. f19), "tayā, anuṣṭup."
"Chandas, by that [meter]—the *anuṣṭubh* meter—by that sit! (4.3.12.f.11–f.20, with a *t*-mantra for each)—[this is the repetition of f.20].

"Evam-chandas" (ibid. f31)—thus from the north—"tayā-yā; varivah-chandas" (ibid. f32), "tayā; vayah-chandas" (ibid. f33), "tayā; vayaskṛt-chandas" (ibid. f34), "tayā; viśālam-chandas" (ibid. f35), "tayā; viṣpardhāḥ-chandas" (ibid. f36), "tayā; chadiḥ-chandas" (ibid. f37), "tayā; dūrohaṇam-chandas" (ibid. f38), "tayā; tandram-chandas" (ibid. f39), "tayā; aṅkākam."

"Chandas, sit down by means of that"—with these thirty-one *stomabhāga* formulas (4.3.12f.31–f.40, each accompanied by its respective *t*-mantra), he extends them on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick: seven in each of the directions and three in the middle. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over each one of those bricks as they touch the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, while they are aligned toward one another.

"Thou art a ray"—with these words he places [the brick] in front: "For dwelling thee; quicken the dwelling. "With that [power], with that... "Thou art a forward-stride; for dharma thee; quicken dharma. "With that [power], with that... "Thou art a following-stride; for heaven thee; quicken heaven. "With that [power], with that... "Thou art a junction; for the intermediate space thee; quicken the intermediate space. "With that [power], with that... "Thou art a forward-stride; for dharma thee... "With that [power], with that... "Thou art a following-stride... (repeated).

"Thou art the repetition for the night; thou art the junction for the intermediate space; thou art the support for the earth; thou art the prop for the rain—for thee! Thou art the forward-blowing for the day; quicken the day—sit down with that! (4.4.1a1–a7, with one *t*-mantra for each)—thus [there are nine mantras, from a1–a4 and a2–a5].

"Thou art the anuvāsī"—thus [he says] from the south—"for the Night thee" (up to the end of the same section), "thou art the Uśij" (4.4.1b2,1)—"for the Night thee," "thou art the Praketa" (4.4.1b3,1)—"for the Night thee," "thou art the Sudīti" (4.4.1b4,1)—"for the Night thee," "thou art the Ojas" (4.4.1b5,1)—"for the Fathers thee," "thou art the Tantus" (4.4.1b6,1)—"for the progeny thee," "thou art the Pṛtanāṣāh" (4.4.1b7,1)—"with thy deity, sit thou. (Each with its respective *t* mantra). Thus [it is said]. (4.4.1b1–b7).

"Revatī asi" (4.4.1c1)—thus [he places] behind; "oṣadhī asi," "abhijit asi," "adhipatiḥ asi," "yantāsi apānāya tvā," "saṃsarpo asi," "vayodhā asi," "trivṛd asi"—with each of these [mantras], he says, "sit thou" (4.4.1c1–c7).

"To the north [he says]: ‘You are increasing (pravṛt); by that deity—[you are] swelling (saṃvṛt); by that—[you are] expanding (vivṛt); by that—you are a joint growth (saṃroha); by that—you are a downward growth (nīroha); by that—you are an upward growth (praroha); by that—you are a subsequent growth (anuroha); by that—sit! (4.4.1d1–d7, with the *tat* mantra for each).

With the formula, “Thou art Vasuko” (4.4.1e,1), he places [the brick] in the middle; then with the formulas, “By that [power], thou art Tayāśrī” (ibid. e,2), “By that [power], thou art Tayāvatī,” and “By that [power], thou art Vasyaṣṭi” (ibid.

e,3)—each accompanied by the *t* mantra—he extends five *nākas* on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, one in each of the cardinal directions, one filled with loose soil (*purīṣavatī*) at the junctions, and one in the middle.

He places one in the east with the formula: "Thou art the queen, the eastern quarter" (4.4.2a,1); "The Vasus are thine, the *Rathantara* Sāman for stability" (ibid., to the end); "For the atmosphere... may they prepare thee" (4.4.2f,1); "With that, sit thou" (4.4.2a & f, with the *t*-mantra). He places one in the south with the formula: "Thou art the sovereign (*virāj*), the southern quarter" (ibid. b,1); "The Rudras are thine, the *Bṛhat* Sāman for stability" (ibid., to the end); "For the atmosphere... (4.4.2f,1)—the rest is the same (4.4.2b & f, with the *t*-mantra).

"To the west: 'Thou art the sovereign (śamrāj), the western quarter'—[the rest] is the same [as in 4.4.2c & f, with the *t* mantra]: 'The Ādityas are thy overlords, the Vairūpa the Sāman for stability, for the intermediate space. To the north:

'Thou art the self-ruler (śvarāj), the northern quarter'—[the rest] is the same [as in 4.4.2d & f, with the *t* mantra]: 'The Viśvedevas are thy overlords, Varuṇa the Sāman, for the intermediate space.'"
"In the middle [he places it] with the formula: *adhipatny asi bṛhatī dik* (4.4.2e,1). With [the formula]: *marutas te sādayantu, tayā devatayā sīda* (4.4.2e & f), he causes them to settle.
He extends these [bricks] above; the wives, having been adorned, adorn these [bricks] with all kinds of fragrant substances."

Having enclosed it with a fence, they bring [the bricks]. He places one in the east with the mantra: "This one in front is the golden-haired, sun-rayed one" (4.4.3a). [He continues: "His two attendants are Rathagṛtsa and Praheti" (ibid., to the end); "to them be homage; may they be gracious to us; I place [him] in the jaw" (4.4.3f); "with that [mantra], sit down" (4.4.3a & f, combined with the *t* mantra).

[Then] in the south with: "This one on the right is Viśvakarman" (4.4.3b). [He continues: "His two attendants are Rathasvana and Praheti" (ibid., to the end); "to them be homage" (4.4.3b & f, combined with the *t* mantra)—this is the same as before.
"This one from the north is Saṃyadvasu" (4.4.3d,1)—thus [he places him] to the north; "and his are Senajit and... to them homage" (4.4.3f)—this is the same [as before];
"This one above is Arvāgvasu" (4.4.3e,1)—thus [he places him] in the middle; "and his are Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi"—the rest is the same (4.4.3e & [mantra]).

"This one behind is Viśvavyacās" (4.4.3c,1)—with this, he places the last brick facing eastward at the back. [K1,62b3] "His [are] Rathaprota and Apraheti; homage to them! May they be gracious to us; I place [the enemy] in their jaws; with that [brick], sit down" (4.4.3c & f, with the *t* mantra).
— Thus [end the sections on] Chandas (28), Vṛṣṭisanī (5), Ādityeṣṭakā (8), and ṅhṛteṣṭakā (5). [K1,62b3–; K4,62b3–; M291–5]

He extends twenty-eight *chandas* verses behind the head-stones: three each directed westward, and one *atichandas* verse. They touch the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone with *dvipadā* verses. He causes the sacrificer to recite over those directed westward; he concludes with those directed northward, beginning with the *gāyatrī* verse, "Agni is the head" (4.4.4a), and "Bhuvaḥ" (4.4.4d).

The *triṣṭubh*s are: “The watchful guardian of the people has been born” (4.4.4g); the *jagatī*s are: “O you of most wondrous fame” (4.4.4k); the *anuṣṭubh*s are: “With this homage to Agni” (4.4.4n); the *bṛhatī*s are: “O Agni, of the booty consisting of cattle” (4.4.4q); and the *uṣṇih* is: “To thee... (4.4.4r).

The *paṅkti* verses are "O Agni, let us kindle thee" (4.4.4t,1) and "O Agni, him today... (4.4.4w,1); he concludes with the *akṣarapaṅkti* verses "Kindle this, O Agni... (4.4.4x,1). The *atichandas* verse is "I honor Agni the Hotṛ, the giver... (4.4.4ā,1), and the *dvipadā* verses are "O Agni, thou art our closest... (4.4.4cc,1). (Cf. BSS 10.45:43.9-14; Tr. p. 569).

He lays down five rain-bringers around the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick: one in each of the quarters and one in the middle. These are placed close together, as it were, without touching one another. He places one in the east with the formula, “Thou art the rain-bringer of the east wind” (4.4.6d1); with the mantra “Sit thou with that,” he places one in the south with the formula, “Thou art the rain-bringer of the clouds” (ibid. d2), followed by the mantra “Sit thou with that.”

With the mantra "thou art the thunderer of lightning" (ibid. 3), he places it to the west; with the mantra "sit down by that," and "thou art the thunderer of the roar" (ibid. 4), to the north; with the mantra "sit down by that," and "thou art the thunderer of rain" (ibid. 5), in the middle; with the mantra "sit down by that."

He lays down eight Āditya bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks, two in each of the quarters, as if they were close together. He places one in the east with the formula: "For the sake of the flood (*śalila*), thee! (4.4.6i1). With the formula: "With that [brick], thee; for the sake of the gathering place (*saṃnikā*), thee! Sit with that! (4.4.6i1i2)—repeating the *tayā sīda* mantra for each—he places one in the south with the formula: "For the sake of the hundred-fold (*śatikā*), thee! (ibid. i3). With the formula: "With that [brick], thee; for the sake of the signal (*ketā*), thee! Sit with that! (4.4.6i3i4)—repeating the *tayā sīda* mantra for each—he places one in the west.

With the formula "For Pracetasa thee" (ibid. i5), he places it to the west; with "For Vivasvat thee" (ibid. 6) and "Sit thereon" (4.4.6i5i6)—repeating the *t* mantra for each—with "For Dyaus thee" (ibid. i7,1?), he places it to the north; and with "For Jyotis thee, for the Ādityas thee" (ibid.
i7,2i8) and "Sit thereon" (4.4.6i7i8)—with a different punctuation than in the Weber edition—repeating the *t* mantra for each.

He lays down five *ghṛteṣṭakā* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, one in each of the quarters and one in the middle; these are laid so as not to touch [the central brick]. He places one in the east with the formula, “For the *ṛc* thee” (*ṛce tvā*) and “Sit with that” (*tayā sīda*);
in the south with “For brilliance thee” (*ruce tvā*) and “Sit with that.”

With "For splendor, thee," [he places it] to the west; with "Sit down with that," [he does so]; with "For brilliance, thee," to the north; with "Sit down with that," [he does so]; with "For light, thee," in the middle; with "Sit down with that," [he does so].

He lays down five *yaśodā* bricks around the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, one in each of the directions and one in the middle; these remain as if close, yet not touching one another. He places one in the east with the mantra: "O *yaśodā*, thee! (VS 4.4.6), followed by: "I settle thee in glory (*yaśas*), by that seer, by that Brahman, by that [deity], do thou sit. (The rest of the mantra is as in verse 1 through its conclusion).

He places one in the south with: "O *tejodā*, thee! (VS 4.4.7), followed by: "I settle thee in splendor (*tejas*), by that seer, by that Brahman, by that [deity], do thou sit. (The rest of the mantra is as above).
With the words, "O giver of milk, thee," [he places it] in the west; with "I set thee in milk;
by that seer, sit!"—with the words, "O giver of luster, thee," in the north; with "I set thee in luster;
by that seer, sit!"—and with the words, "O giver of wealth, thee," in the middle; with "I set thee in wealth; by that seer, by that sacred formulation (brahman)..."
With the formula, "Sit down by means of her," he extends five *bhūyaskṛt* bricks all around the *svayamātṛṇṇā*; one in each of the directions. These remain as if not touching one another.
With the formula, "Thou art the *bhūyaskṛt*," he places one in the east; with the formula, "Sit down by means of her," [he places another].
With the words "Thou art the maker of wide space" (4.4.7a2), he places [the stone] to the south; with "Sit with that," [he does so].

With "Thou art the eastern one" (4.4.7a3), he places it to the west; with "Sit with that," [he does so]. With "Thou art the upward one" (4.4.7a4), he places it to the north; with "Sit with that," [he does so].
"Thou art seated in the intermediate space; sit in the intermediate space"—with these words he places it in the middle.
With "sit with that," he extends the form of the five fires. ... the bricks become one by one... He places it in front with "Thou art seated in the waters" (4.4.7b1), and with "sit with that."

With the words, "Thou art seated like a hawk," he places it to the south; with "Sit thou here with that," [he does so]; with "Thou art seated like a vulture," he places it to the west; with "Sit thou here with that," and with "Thou art seated like a falcon," he places it to the north; with "Sit thou here with that."

With the formula, “Thou art the one who dwells in the sky,” he places [one brick] in the middle; with “Sit down by that,” he arranges five *draviṇodās* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*. He places one on each side... [with the formula] “I settle thee in wealth” (4.4.7c1), he lays it down in the east; with “Sit down by that,” and “I settle thee in the wealth of the intermediate space” (ibid. c2), he places it in the south; with “Sit down by that,”... [he places it in the west].
"To the direction of heaven I settle you for wealth"—thus [he says] from behind; "with that sit down.
"To the direction of the intermediate space I settle you for wealth"—thus from the north; "with that sit down."

"O giver of wealth, I settle thee in wealth"—thus [he places it] in the middle. With "sit down with that," he extends the threads... He causes [the sacrificer] to recite over the *pū*... the *haṃsapātinī* threads directed toward the north: "Protect my out-breath, sit with that; protect my in-breath, sit with that; protect my diffused breath, sit with that; protect my life-span, sit with that; protect my all-encompassing life-span, sit with that; protect my complete life-span, sit with that; O Agni, that which is thine..."
He lays down seven *dantī* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*. One each in the quarters, three in the middle; these are as if close together, yet they remain untouched [by one another].
He places one in the east with the formula, “*yāvā*, sit thou with her”;
in the south he places one with “*ayāvā*, sit thou with her.”

With the words "evā," he places one behind; with "tayā sīda" and "ūmā," one to the north; with "tayā sīda" and "śabda," one in the middle; and with "tayā yā, sā... dakas tayā sīda," he settles them. He extends the *jyānīs* on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*; there is one in each of the directions and one in the middle, and they touch one another.

One should place the *rāṣṭrabhṛt* bricks first for a Kṣatriya. One places them in the east with the formula: “For him whose weapons are a hundred,” “For him whose strength is a hundred,” and “O all-encompassing one, sit here with her.

In the south, with the formula: “The four paths... In the west, with the formula: “Summer, winter... may we be in safety through her, sit here with her. In the north, with the formula: “May we be in safety through her, sit here with her.”
With the formula, "For the *idu*-year—may we be unharmed through her; sit down with her," he places one to the north.
With the formula, "The gods have led us from good to better," he places one in the middle. With the formula, "Through you, O dwelling, may it be pleasant;

sit down with her," he lays down four *rāṣṭrabhṛt* (sovereignty-sustaining) bricks on all sides around the *svayamātṛṇṇā* stone, one in each direction, so that they are as if close together yet remain untouched by one another.
He places [the brick] in the east with: "O glorious Agni... [and] "...may he be endowed with glory; may he have Indra as his companion; may there be a supreme hymn for him;

sit thou here with that. He places it in the south with: "Beholding what is auspicious... [and] "...they approached in the beginning; may they bow down; sit thou here with that. [And he places it] with:
"The Ordainer, the Disposer... and so forth.
Afterwards, with the verses, "The supreme one... let them bow down to you... sit down" (*paramas ta...* etc.

and "Turn back toward us" (*abhyāvartadhvam*), he places twelve *bhūteṣṭakā* bricks to the north with the verse, "All together... sit down" (*upametasāka...* etc.). He places them on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks, three in each direction; he places a ladle of clarified butter (*ājyasthālī*) touching each one of those *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks.

With the formula, “For the earth thee” (*śruvañ ca pṛthivyai tvā*), he places it in front of the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick so that it does not touch it. With the formula, “By that deity; for the earth, svāhā,” he offers an oblation with the *sruva* ladle upon the *svayamātṛṇṇā*.

With the formula, “For the intermediate space thee; by that [deity]; for the intermediate space, svāhā,” he offers an oblation with the *sruva* ladle upon the *svayamātṛṇṇā*. With the formula, “For the sky thee; by that [deity]; for the sky, svāhā,” [he offers].
He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For Sūrya thee!"—thus he places [the brick] to the south, touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* [brick], saying, "Thou art; for Sūrya, svāhā! (1.8.13i4).
He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For Candramas thee! Thou art; for Candramas, svāhā! (1.8.13i5).
He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For the Nakṣatras thee! Thou art; for the Nakṣatras, svāhā! (1.8.13i6).

He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For the waters, thee!"—then he places [a brick] touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* from behind, saying, "For those [waters], thee! To the waters, svāhā! (1.8.13i7).
He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For the plants, thee! For those [plants], thee! To the plants, svāhā! (1.8.13i8).
He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying, "For the trees, thee! For those [trees], thee! To the trees, svāhā! (1.8.13i9).

He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying: "For the moving and the unmoving, thee!"—he places it to the north, touching the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick, saying: "With that [brick], for the moving and the unmoving, svāhā!
(1.8.13i10). He offers with the *sruva*-ladle, saying: "For the wandering ones, thee!"—"With that [brick], for the wandering ones, svāhā! (1.8.13i11).
With the formula, "Svāhā to the reptiles for you!
(1.8.13i12), he offers an oblation into the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick using the *sruva* ladle.
Regarding this, it is said: "Let that Brāhmaṇa who knows the *brāhmaṇavatī* brick place it here."

Then these bricks are laid down: the Śūrpa, the Ūrdhva-yajñī, the Saṃpā, the Svarita, the Pañcajanīyas, and the Sarvatomukha. The Brāhmaṇas lay down the bricks according to their respective Vedic texts. Then he extends these three bricks, which have the form of the Vedas, at the end toward the north, in front of the Svayamātṛṇṇā brick. He causes [the sacrificer] to recite the Haṃsapātinī verses while facing northward: "With the *vaṣaṭ*-call I lay thee down with the Ṛg; sit thou with her! With the *pratigara* I lay thee down with the Yajus; sit thou with her! With the *hiṅkāra* I lay thee down with the Sāman; sit thou with her!"
He lays down twelve womb-bricks with the verse, “O Agni, whose branch we meditate upon as our hymn of praise” (*agne yasya stomam manāmahe*).
Having laid down the layer (*citi*), he joins it together with the formula, “Today, may that which reaches the sky of the god Draviṇas succeed; sit down with that.
He touches it with the mantra, “The conscious [layer], the unconscious [layer]” (*cittim acittim*), and with the mantra, “By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.”
Right here he pours out the loose soil for him;
having piled it up in the afternoon, he lays it down with the verse, "He who is asked in heaven" (VS 4.4.12q; TS 1.5.11d; TB 3.7.11.6).

With the formula, "By that, O God, sit down," he touches [the altar] with the verse, "The conscious and the unconscious. Then, with the formula, "By that, sit down," he arranges these layers (*citi*): the *vibhaktis*, the *saṃyatas*, the *jyotiṣmatīs*, the *nakṣatreṣṭakās*, the *āvapanam*, the *vikarṇyas*, the *maṇḍaleṣṭakā*, the *hiraṇyeṣṭakā*, the *sandhis*, the touching, the *paṅkti-āgā*, the oblation of the *hotṛ*, the descent, and the attendance. This constitutes his ritual duty.
He pronounces the *vibhakti* with the word "O Agni! (*agne*).
Then he lays down these *saṃyata* bricks on both sides of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*s—two in each of the quarters and two in the middle. These remain as if close together, yet untouched.

He places them in the east with the formula: "The Restrainer and the Forethoughtful; of Agni, Soma, and Sūrya—these are your overlords; homage to them! May they be gracious to us! Sit ye two in the firm foundation! (TS 4.4.11.2h, 3n).

Saying, “The fierce and the terrible,” he makes an offering to the south, pronouncing: “Of the ancestors, of Yama, of Indra—these are your overlords; homage to them! (TS 4.4.11.3n). Saying, “The firm and the earth,” he makes an offering to the west, pronouncing: “Of the god Savitṛ, of the Maruts, of Varuṇa—these are your overlords; homage to them! (TS 4.4.11.3n).
"Both Dhartrī and Dharitrī"—thus to the north, [the offering] for Mitra and Varuṇa, for the element of Mitra; "they are your overlords, homage to them"—this is the same [formula].
"Both Prācī and Pratīcī"—thus in the middle, for the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas; "they are your overlords... I place [it] in the jaw, by that... sit ye both."

He causes the *jyotiṣmatī* bricks to be brought from the east; he causes the *haṃsapātinī* bricks to be placed toward the north while reciting: "I settle thee, the luminous one—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the light-maker—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the finder of light—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the radiant one—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the blazing one—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the shimmering one—*ta=yā*; I settle thee, the shining one..."

With the formula, "Thee, the shining ones, I settle; thee, the unceasing ones, I settle; thee, the ones of great light, I settle; thee, the awakening ones, I settle; thee, the watchful ones, I settle—with that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm!"—he places the Nakṣatra bricks around the Svayamātṛṇṇā on all sides, those belonging to the head on the south side, and he places the Pūrṇamāsī brick.
To the west of that, having arranged the seven *kṛttikās* in a circle like a heap, not touching one another, he extends a single line through their center; to the west of that, he extends *rohiṇī*.

He extends these toward the west: *mṛgaśīrṣa*, *ārdrā*, the two *punarvasūs*, *tiṣya*, *āśleṣā*, *maghā*, the two *phalgunīs*, *hasta*, *citrā*, *svātī*, and the two *viśākhe*. To the south of the *svayamātṛṇṇā*, he extends [the line].
To the west, he lays out the Svayamātṛṇṇā and the Ekāṣṭakā;

to the north of it, he lays out the Anūrādhās. He lays these out facing east: two Agnis, two Aṣāḍhās, Śroṇā, Śraviṣṭhās, Śatabhiṣaj, the Proṣṭhapadas, the Proṣṭhapadas, Revatī, the two Aśvayujas, and the Bharaṇīs. To the north, he lays out the Amāvāsyā among the stars of the head.
With the words, “The full [moon] afterwards” (TS 4.4.10.3c1), he lays down the Paurṇamāsī brick with the formula: “And the full [moon], making them rejoice; through her, sit thou.”

With the words, “Thou art Ambā by name” (*TS* 4.4.5.1b1; cf. *BĀU* 10.45:43.14; *AP* 17.5.4), he places the first of the seven *Kṛttikās* while stepping forward: “I place thee with Prajāpati and with all holy thoughts; thou art Dulā by name. With Prajāpati and [the same mantra], “Thou art Nitatni by name. With Prajāpati and [the same mantra], “Thou art Abhrayantī by name. With Prajāpati and [the same mantra], “Thou art Meghayantī by name. With Prajāpati and [the same mantra].

"You are named Varṣayantī; by Prajāpati I lay you down with all the *dhītis*; through that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!"—thus [he says]. "You are named Pupūṇīkā"—thus [he says] in the middle—"by Prajāpati... sit"—thus [he says].
"The *nakṣatra* is Kṛttikā"—with these words, he lays down all of them together.

"Fire is the deity; you are the luster of Agni, of Prajāpati, of Dhātṛ, of Soma—with that, sit down"—with these words he covers them with the verse, "For your luster, for your brilliance, for your radiance, for your light—with that, sit down firm.
With the formula, "Rohiṇī is the asterism," he places the Rohiṇī brick, saying, "Prajāpati is the deity; with that, sit down."
With the words, "For the Ṛc, thee! (4.4.10.1a2), he covers it [with a cloth], saying: "For brilliance, thee; for splendor, thee; for luster, thee; for light, thee; with that, sit down."

In this very way, he recites over these [constellations] up to the two Viśākhās: "Mṛgaśīrṣa is the lunar mansion; Soma is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Ārdrā is the lunar mansion; Rudra is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Punarvasū are the lunar mansions; Aditi is their deity. By them—by those [deities]. Tiṣya is the lunar mansion; Bṛhaspati is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Āśleṣās are the lunar mansions; the Serpents are their deities. By them—by those [deities]. Maghās are the lunar mansions; Pūṣan is their deity. By them—by those [deities]. Phalgunī is the lunar mansion; Aryaman is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Phalgunī is the lunar mansion; Bhaga is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Hasta is the lunar mansion; Savitṛ is its deity. By it—by that [deity]. Citrā is the lunar mansion."

"Indra is its deity; Svātī is the constellation, Vāyu is its deity; Viśākhā is the constellation, Indra and Agni are its deities—with that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm!"—with this he covers [the brick] with the verse, "For splendor for you" (TS 4.4.10.1a, var.), saying: "For brilliance for you, for radiance for you, for light for you, for luster for you—with that, sit ye both firm!"—with the formula, "The Ekāṣṭakā" (TS 4.3.11.3h), he lays down the Ekāṣṭakā brick, saying: "Tormented by austerity, through her powers—with that, sit thou firm!"—thus.

He lays down the Anurādhas with the words, "The asterism Anurādhā" (TS 4.4.10.2b14–26): "Mitra is the deity; by him [the asterism Rohiṇī]; Indra is the deity; by him [the asterism Viśṛta]; the Pitṛs are the deity; by them [the asterism Aṣāḍhā]; the Viśve Devas are the deity; by them [the asterism Śroṇā]; Śraviṣṭhā is the asterism; by them [the asterism Śraviṣṭhā]; Indra is the deity; by him [the asterism Śatabhiṣaj]; the Proṣṭhapadas are the asterism; by them [the asterism Proṣṭhapada]; the Proṣṭhapadas are the asterism; by them [the asterism Proṣṭhapada]."

"Revatī is the lunar mansion; Pūṣan is its deity. With that deity, sit down! Aśvayuj is the lunar mansion; the Aśvins are its deity. With that deity, sit down! Apabharaṇī is the lunar mansion; Yama is its deity. With that deity, sit down!"—with these words he lays down the Amāvāsyā brick. Then, with the verse, "That which the gods bestowed upon thee... (TS 4.4.10.3c2 < TS 3.5.1.1b), he lays down the Amāvāsyā brick, saying: "The portion for the Amāvāsyā is well-heroic; with that, sit down! At this point, he should lay down the Surūpā brick.
If they should thus deviate excessively, they lay down twelve womb-bricks (*yonīḥ*).

They make the bricks well-provided with openings for Agni... and [with the formula] "O Rudra... and so forth; from the seven [verses] they make the spaces (*ākāśān*), and having placed the *lokaṃpṛṇā* and the branches...
Then he places these four *svayamātṛṇṇā* bricks in the quarters, in their respective directions:
with the formula "For breath thee" (TS 5.5.5.4) in the east, and with "For sight thee; by that sit thou" in the other directions.

With the formula, “For the vyāna-breath you,” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5.5.5.4), he places it to the south; with “For the eye you, sit there with that,” and “For the apāna-breath you,” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5.5.5.4), he places it to the west; with “For the eye you, sit there with that,” and “For speech you,” (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5.5.5.4), he places it to the north; and with “For the eye you, sit there with that.”

With the mantra, “The sky is pervaded by the unconquered immortality” (TS 4.4.5.2e), he places a Maṇḍaleṣṭakā brick, touching it to the western end of the Svayamātṛṇṇā, with the formula, “May the Ādityas be your guardians; may Sūrya be your guardian; sit down with her.

With the mantra, “Thou art the light” (TS 5.7.6.1–2c3), he places a Hiraṇyeṣṭakā brick upon this one, with the formula, “Grant me the light; grant me the sky; protect me from the sky; sit down with her.”

Having laid down the layer with the words, "The mortal who [offers] worship," he joins [the layers] together with the verses beginning, "They, rejoicing with their praises, have come for help at the rising of the dawn; sit down with that one.
He touches [the altar] with the verse, "The conscious and the unconscious" (TS 5.5.4.4), namely, "Sit down with that one.
With the *paṅkti* verse, "O Agni, him today... (4.4.4.7), he touches it, saying, "...as [one honors] horses with hymns and offerings; sit down with that one."

With the formula, "May you live for all your life," he takes up the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick. Then the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer both recite the sacrificial formula: "I set you down in the seat of Ayu with curds. He stops with the words, "In the shade, with most peaceful shelter. To the north, the Pratiprasthātṛ lays down the *vikarṇī* brick with the formula, "When there is great blackness... (4.4.3.3i).
Both perform the *tayādevata* rite together with the formula, "With that [brick], sit down. Having laid it down with the word "Heaven," he breathes over it with the *anvapa* formula.
He may grant a boon to the Adhvaryu as he desires.

With the words, “I have ascended to heaven” (5.6.8.1a3), he steps upon it with his two thumbs; with the words, “We have gone to the light” (śuvar aganma)—and [reciting] “I offer consciousness” (cittiṃ juhomi) (5.5.4.3)—he offers four ladlings into it. Having offered the oblation of the seven-hotṛ with the mind, saying, “The Prastotṛ has sung the Sāman,” and having performed the offering for the seven-hotṛ, saying, “Giver of out-breath, giver of in-breath... homage to thee,” they remain performing the service for the highest layer (city).
In the morning, having released his speech with the *āditya* [verse], he ascends the *pravargya* vessel;
then he lays down the "asked" (*pṛṣṭa*) bricks in the sky.
He does not perform the *tayādevata* offering;
he merely touches [the altar] with the words, "The conscious, the unconscious" (5.5.4.4),
and does not perform the *tayādevata* offering at all.
Having descended, he ascends again;
then, with the formula, "O Agni, of the forest" (5.5.9.1e), he offers an oblation of loose earth (*purīṣa*). With the formula, "That arrow of thine which...
he descends and scatters a thousand pieces of gold into a vessel of water.
Standing to the west of the fire, he sprinkles it with the formula, “Thou art the measure of a thousand” (TS 4.4.11.3o [var]), saying, “The measure of a thousand—for a thousand thee.
Having gone around the fire to the south, he touches those bricks which rise up from the middle toward the head with the formula, “May these bricks, O Agni, be milch-cows” (TS 4.4.11.3p1 [var?]).
He then proceeds along the path back with the formulas, “One and a hundred” (TS 4.4.11.3–4p2), and “A thousand and the further half.”

Having gone around the fire to the north, he touches them with the mantra: “O Agni, may these bricks of mine be milch-cows” (TS 4.4.11.4p3). With the mantra: “Sixty thousand self-sustaining ones” (4.4.11.4p4), and “May those bricks of mine, O Agni, be milch-cows” (cf. TS 4.4.11.4p5 [variant]), having gone around by the same northern path, he touches those very same bricks with the mantra: “The Vijrājas by name—in that world and here.”

Having made the cows [the objects of worship], he worships them with the *saṃhāra* and *vihāra* formulas: "Thou art the *Śaṃvatsara*, thou art the *Parivatsara*, thou art the *Idāvatsara*; bring us the greatness of that [year] of thine; O Vāyu, having become the *dhāmacchandas*, bring all the quarters according to our desire.
Having worshipped with the *saṃhāra* and *vihāra* formulas and having performed the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites, he performs these two again during the day alone.
[The *Zatatarudrīya*].

Now he explains this ritual of the Śatarudrīya: a leaf of the *arka* plant, goat’s milk, groats of wild sesame (*jartila*), a porridge of *gavīdhuka* seeds, a bow, three arrows, a water-jar, a stone, a water-vessel, a branch of reed (*vetasa*), *avakā* plants, a frog, and a long bamboo pole.

Having mixed the wild sesame groats with goat’s milk, he places them in his left hand upon an *arka* leaf and begins the rite while holding [the materials] at knee-height, reciting over the last brick of the northern wing: "Homage to you, O Rudra, to your wrath" (TS 4.5.1a).
Having recited, "Homage to the armies and to the army-leaders, homage to you! (4.5.4k), he makes the sound "vaṭ.
Then, while holding [the staff] at the height of the navel, he proceeds, having recited, "Homage to the attendants and to the collectors, homage to you!
(*ibid* l), and makes the sound "vaṭ" after reciting, "Homage to the one of the wells and to the one of the pits! (4.5.7l).
Saying, “Obeisance to those who rain and to those who do not rain” (ibid.), he begins while holding [the vessel] at the height of the neck.
Having uttered, “We sacrifice to as many as there are” (*Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 4.5.11.2k), he makes the sound “vaṭ.

Having said, “Come, O sacrificer,” while the sacrificer has taken hold of him, he causes the sacrificer to recite the final deity: “Obeisance to the Rudras who are in heaven” (ibid.; cf. *Taittirīya Saṃhitā* p. 581, n. 136). He begins while holding [the vessel] at the height of the neck.
"To those whose rain is the arrow, to them I assign ten eastern [arrows] and ten for the jaw"—having recited this (from *Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 4.5.11.2 to the end), he makes the sound "vaṭ.
Holding [the bow] at the height of the navel, he proceeds with the formula: "Obeisance to the Rudras who are in the intermediate space" (*Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 4.5.11.2).
"Salutation to those whose arrows are the winds—to them [be homage]" (ibid., to the end), thus reciting, he proceeds while holding [the vessel] at knee-height with the formula:
"Salutation to the Rudras who are on the earth" (4.5.11.2). Then, holding it at waist-height, he proceeds with:

"To those whose food is the arrows—to them [be homage]" (ibid., to the end)—"I place ten in the east, ten in the south, ten in the west, ten in the north; I place ten above, ten below, ten in the intermediate directions, and ten in the jaws. (ibid., to the end).
He makes the sound "vaḍ.

Upon the final brick of this very same layer (*pakṣa*), he places an offering of *gāvīdhuka* grain, reciting the verse, "The Rudra who is in the fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants" (*Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa* 5.5.9.3i), ending with "The Rudra who is in all [beings]—let there be homage" (*ibid.*, to the end).
He makes the sound "vaḍ."
Regarding this, [it is said]: "One should deposit this upon the path of one whom he hates, among his cattle" (Śrautasūtra 5.4.3.5; cf. Baudhāyana Śrautasūtra 10.48:49.4–5).
That [deposition] is performed with a leaf of the *arka* tree.
He takes up the bow and three arrows with the mantra, "O Rudra, that bow which you held in front... (TS 5.5.7.2–3).
Standing to the west of the fire, he addresses the quarters: "It has been directed toward the quarters; to that I pay homage through the wind for a year" (ibid.).
Taking a water-pot, the sprinkler gives that unasked gift to the Brāhmaṇa; going around three times while sprinkling from left to right,
he sprinkles with the words, "Strength in the stone" (TS 4.6.1.1a).
He causes [the priest] to recite, "On the mountain, rejoicing" (ibid., end), and with the words,
"May hunger be in the stone for thee" (4.6.1.1b, 1), he touches the jar with a stone;
then, with the words, "In that [stone], we hate thee" (ibid., end), he pours the contents of the jar onto the stone.
Whatever the sacrificer hates, that he meditates upon while sprinkling water around [the fire].

Without looking back, they return and tie a reed branch (*vetasa*), a blade of grass (*avaka*), and a frog onto a long bamboo pole with the mantra: "With the *avakā* plant of the ocean... (4.6.1.1c). Standing behind the fire, he draws [the pole] across with eight verses, beginning with "To our sacrifice and oblation... (4.6.1.3k, end).
As soon as he approaches that long bamboo pole, the fire is extinguished; having drawn it away from his desire, the Adhvaryu leads the Udgātṛ forward, establishing him with Sāmans.

He worships it from the front with the Gāyatra, the southern wing with the Rathantara, and the northern wing with the Bṛhat, thereby making it full of vigor; he worships the tail with the Yajñāyajñiya.
One who has maintained the *saṃvatsara* sacrifice for a year should perform it while established in the seasons:

the middle [of the body] with the *vāmadevya*, the right shoulder with the *vāravantīya*, the left shoulder with the *śyaita*, the right wing with the *Prajāpater hṛdaya*, the left [wing] with the *agner vrata*, and the head with the *agner arka*. Having sat down to the west of the fire with the words, "Father Mātariśvan" (5.6.8.6), the *hotṛ* recites the *anuśaṃsana* of the chant, beginning with "Unbroken steps, he shall establish... (up to the end of [h]1).

With the verse, "The sacrifice has been performed by the Vasus" (*TS 5.6.8g, 1 with variant), the Brahman makes the sacrificer recite the *doha* (milk-yielding formula) for the *stotra* and *śastra*, ending with "May I obtain the fulfillment of my prayers" (*āśīrdā bhakṣīya*).

Having ascended [the cart] and taken five portions of clarified butter, he offers an oblation of the five *śāpāla* stalks with the formula, "Thou art named Samīcī, the eastern quarter," and releases these six [stalks].
Having offered oblations to one of these guardians of the quarters, they dwell there.

He offers four *rauhiṇa* cakes cooked in milk. There are five portions of clarified butter (*ājya*), two portions of curds mixed with honey, a handful of *grumuṣṭi* grass, two oblations from the *sruva*-ladle, two portions of fourfold-drawn butter, three fuel-sticks of *udumbara* wood, a speckled stone for sprinkling the clarified butter, an *udumbara* vessel full of curds, three *udumbara* fuel-sticks, one of *vikaṅkata*, one of *śamī*, and one of *vaiśvakarmaṇī* wood; a *pañkti*-verse offering, a full-oblation (*pūrṇāhuti*), a cake on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara, and a cake on seven potsherds.

A jar of clarified butter for the wind-god, a large-handled ladle, all kinds of herbs, a wooden spoon made of *udumbara* wood, the fourteen *vājaprasavīya* formulas, the six *pārtha* offerings, the six *bhūtānām aveṣṭayaḥ*, a black antelope skin, and the consecration—these are the six *pārtha* offerings, the six *bhūtānām aveṣṭayaḥ*, the milk of a black cow with a white calf, the two *rāṣṭrabhṛt* offerings, then the names of the winds, five *arka* oblations, verses addressed to Varuṇa, three *agnihotra* oblations, and nine *samiṣṭayajus* formulas; this constitutes his ritual performance.
Having released his speech with the *āditya* formula and having performed the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites, as he steps out, he says: "Give the half-vow (*ardhavratam*)!
Running forward while performing these three acts, the Adhvaryu causes the sacrificer to consume the vow-food (*vratayati*), and the sacrificer follows after him.

When he has arrived, the Adhvaryu pours the fivefold-drawn ghee transversely across the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick with the *paṅkti* verse: "To the one seated on the Ṛṣis, vaṭ! To the one seated in the waters, vaṭ! To the one who has found heaven, vaṭ! (4.6.1.3n). Thus it is said.

With the formula, “Ye devā devānām” (4.6.1.3o–p), he sprinkles the fire with curds mixed with honey using two handfuls of *grumuṣṭi* grass. With the formula, “The sacrificial ones of the sacrificial ones, belonging to the year...

upon the summit” (ibid., end of p), having made the fire shaped like a male tortoise and placed the *grumuṣṭi* on its northern side, he offers six oblations to the guardians of the quarters with the other curds mixed with honey, using the formula, “Hētayas by name you are” (5.5.10.3c, 1).
Having descended from the sacrificial ground, he proceeds with the *pravargya* and *upasad* rites; he concludes the *pravargya* according to the prescribed procedure.
Having offered the oblation to Sūrya, they set fire to the fuel and proceed.

When the fuel has been reached, he takes four spoonfuls of clarified butter and offers a spoon-oblation before the fourfold portion with the verse, "Agni with his sharp flame... (ŚB 4.6.1.5), ending with "whatever wealth, svāhā" (as above, ending with *svāhā*).

With the verse, “He who, offering up all these worlds... (4.6.2.1a), he begins the Vaiśvakarman oblation using four ladlefuls (*caturgṛhīta*). With the first half of the hymn, “By Viśvakarman he was born, the god... he established [them] in many places, svāhā” (4.6.2.3–4h, with *svāhā*), he offers a spoonful (*sruvāhuti*) prior to the four ladlefuls, concluding with, “O you who are well-disposed toward us, shine upon us with wealth, svāhā. (To the end, with *svāhā*. He recites, “With this army... (TS 4.3.13.2e).
With the words, “The father of the eye, for he is wise in mind” (4.6.2.4i,1), he begins the Vaiśvakarman offering with four spoonfuls.

With the northern half of the hymn, “To the ocean, the one who knows the way—*svāhā* to the oblation” (4.6.2.6r, with *svāhā*), he offers. He places three pieces of *udumbara* wood with the verse, “Lead him upward, O Agni,” and with the formula, “Oblated with ghee and with wealth—*svāhā*” (4.6.3.1a, with *svāhā*).

With the verse, “Upwards thee all the gods” (4.6.3.1–2d), he lifts up the fire with one [verse]. While they lift it up with the words, “O Agni, let them bring [thee]—the radiant one” (ibid., to the end), they place the fuel and the supporting ladles (*upayamanī*).

He says, “Recite for the fire as it is being carried forward. Then the Adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite: “With the single wooden sword, running after, not resisting, in thy prayer... [10?]... the sacrifice... do not overstep the path.”
With the verse, “*Āśuḥ śiśānaḥ* (TS 4.6.4a.1),” the Brahman priest begins the *Apratiratha* hymn.

With the six verses beginning with, “May the five divine quarters protect the sacrifice” (TS 4.6.3e–i), he strikes [the post]; he concludes with, “Thence may the purifying blessings be pleased with us” (TS 4.6.3i, end).

"This celestial chariot stands in the midst of heaven" (4.6.3.3–4k,1); [thus... he places the curd-mixed [oblation] with the words, "He has filled the two worlds" (ibid., 2) and "He guards the ends of the mid-region" (4.6.3.4 l, end) (4.6.3k–l).

With the four verses beginning, "All have magnified Indra" (4.6.3.4m,1) (4.6.3m–p), he proceeds as far as the tail, [reciting] "Of oceanic extent" (4.6.3m,2) and "May they scatter them in all directions" (4.6.3p, end).

Taking the clarified butter for sprinkling, while standing to the west of the fire, he sprinkles it with the formula: "May the Vasus protect you from the east with the Rudras" (TS 5.5.9.1); then with "May the Pitṛs and Yama [protect you] from above" (ibid., end);

and with "Go forth, O wise one, toward the eastern quarter" (TS 4.6.5.1a), taking a ladle made of Udumbara wood filled with curds, he steps over [the fire] with the five verses beginning with "May the sacrificers go to heaven in safety" (TS 4.6.5.2e).
He recites the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the Audumbarī offering: "Night and Dawn" (4.6.5.2f, 1), ending with "of different forms, bestowing wealth" (ibid., to the end).
He offers the oblation with: "O Agni, thousand-eyed" (4.6.5.2-3g, 1), ending with "hundred-headed, for strength, *svāhā*" (ibid., to the end).

While the fuel-stick is being held, having offered into the fire, he pours [the remains] into the *svayamātṛṇṇā* brick with three verses: "Thou art the fair-winged Garuḍa" (4.6.5.3h,1); he settles [the vessel] with "Sit upon the earth" (ibid., 2)—and "And sit, O sacrificer" (ibid., i, end)—and with "Sit down, O Hotṛ" (4.1.3.3k,1; cf. 3.5.11f,1; cf. 5.1.4.5). On the following day, he scatters the supporting ashes with "In the world, may we place the vigor" (ibid., to the end).
He deposits the fire with the formula, "O Prajāpati, [protect]... svāhā.
Having descended and taking up the wooden sword (sphya), he says, "Step aside; let me not enclose you."

"O Brahman, I shall perform the northern tracing (parigrāha),"—thus he instructs the Brahman while standing to the south of the fire. Once authorized, having propped up [the post] to the north and standing to the east of the hall, he issues the command: "Place the sprinkling waters! (prokṣaṇīr āsādaya).

They bring for him the sprinkling waters; he places down the fuel and the sacrificial grass; he sprinkles the fuel and the sacrificial grass; having come while spreading a bundle of grass for rain, he steps upon it even as he approaches.
"O Agni, kindled, shine before us" (4.6.5.4k,1)— with this verse he places the Audumbara branch, [concluding] with "unfailing strength, svāhā" (ibid., at the end, with *svāhā*).

With the mantra, "We would worship thee at thy highest birth, O Agni" (4.6.5.4 l, 1), he takes a fuel-stick of *vaikaṅkata* wood; with "We would worship [thee] when kindled, svāhā" (at the end of the same passage, with *svāhā*), he takes one of *śamī* wood;
and with "I choose that wonderful [splendor] of the desirable Savitṛ... svāhā" (at the end of the same passage, with *svāhā*), he draws four portions of clarified butter.

He offers that [oblation] with the verse addressed to Viśvakarman: "I offer consciousness" (5.5.4.3,1; cf. 5.7.4.1a), followed by "with mind and ghee—oblation, svāhā! (ibid., at the end, with *svāhā*).
Then he takes another fourfold portion [of ghee] with the *paṅkti* verse: "O Agni, him today... (4.4.4w,1; cf. 5.7.4.1b), ending with "like horses with hymns—offerings, svāhā! (ibid., at the end).

Furthermore, he takes four portions; having filled [the ladle], he offers the full oblation with the mantra: "Seven [are] yours, O Agni, with ghee, svāhā! (TS 4.6.5.5n; cf. 5.4.7.5; also 1.5.2.4; 1.5.3.2).

While offering, he should meditate on the quarters with his mind (TS 5.4.7.6). They bring [the portions] for him—those spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over—with the call: "The Vaiśvānara [portion] first, the Māruta [portions]; recite the invitatory verse for the Vaiśvānara! he says.
Placing the oblation, which has been spread with base-ghee and sprinkled with top-ghee, for Vaiśvānara, the Hotṛ alone recites the invitatory verse for this;
the Hotṛ sacrifices. He says, "O Śrauṣaṭ," and "Sacrifice to Vaiśvānara";
when the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation.
The Hotṛ sits down;
having run after the group with the group, the Adhvaryu offers the Māruta oblations in a low voice (*upāṃśu*),
and he takes the first of these, which has been spread with a base of ghee and sprinkled over.
He recites, “*sabharasa* (TS 4.6.5.6t2),” and [continues] with, “May the Maruts be followers in this sacrifice” (end of ibid.).
He performs the *iḍā*-offering with, “*īdṛṅ ca* (TS 4.6.5.5o,1),” and he recites this:
“*anyādṛṅ ca etādṛṅ ca sabharā*” (ibid., to the end).
He sacrifices with the formula, “And Śukrajyotis” (ŚB 4.6.5.5); he recites this [verse], “And Citrajyotis, O Aṃhasaspati” (ibid.);
and he sacrifices with the formula, “And Ṛtajit” (ŚB 4.6.5.6).
He recites this [verse]: "And the one who conquers truth, and the one from whom the enemy is far away" (ibid., end);
he sacrifices with the *araṇye'nuvākyā* and recites the *araṇye'nuvākyā*:
"And Truth" (4.6.5.6r,1)—thus he sacrifices.
He recites this [verse]: "And being true, may we worship" (*ibid.*, with variations, to the end);
he sacrifices with "Such as these" (4.6.5s,1); he recites this [verse]: "With such aids as these" (*ibid.*, to the end of *t1*).
He offers with the formula, “śabharasa” (ŚB 4.6.5.6), and takes four spoonfuls with the formula, “May the Maruts be followers” (Ibid. t2 to the end & Ibid. u to the end).
They fix two long-handled sacrificial ladles (*sruc*) made of *ājyakuṃbha* wood upon two pillars on either side of the southern hip of the altar;
they either erect a bamboo pole across these two or support it.

Having raised this ladle, he offers the *vasordhārā* (stream of wealth) oblation with the mantra: "O Agni and Viṣṇu, being of one accord... (4.7.1.1a), ending with: "...may these increase for us; come, svāhā! (ibid., with *svāhā*).
They pour from the jar of clarified butter into a large-handled ladle, and a continuous stream of *vasordhārā* flows forth.

He begins with the twelfth [verse]: “*vājaś ca me prasavaś ca me*. He offers oblations at each of the twelve [verses], without pausing. Then, having paused as he desires, he offers the final twelfth [verse] with a distinct break: “*vājāya svāhā*.”

[51] Having offered oblations into the butter-pitcher with the formulas: “To *prasava* svāhā! To *apijā* svāhā! To *kratu* svāhā! To *sū* svāhā! To the *mūrdhan* svāhā! To the *vyaśniya* svāhā! To the *antyāyana* svāhā! To the *antya* svāhā! To the *bhauvana* svāhā! To the *bhuvana* svāhā! To the *adhipati* svāhā!”—he pours clarified butter over all the medicinal herbs.

He mixes [the grains] with curds of every kind, saying, "The impulse of strength has impelled this one at the beginning" (1.7.10a). With a ladle made of udumbara wood, he offers fourteen oblations related to the impulse of strength (*vājaprasavīya*), beginning with "I release peace for myself" (4.7.12.2g). He offers the fourteenth with a vessel (*pātrī*). He pours out [the remainder] with the ladle.

With the formula, "For sprinkling, with milk, with ghee, may I unite myself; may I win the waters, O Agni, svāhā! (repeating this up to the end, each time with "svāhā"), he offers six oblations pertaining to the earth.
The *aveṣṭi* of the elements consists of six offerings: "To Agni, svāhā! (1.8.13h1) and so forth are for the earth; "To Pṛthivī, svāhā! (1.8.13i1) and so forth is the *aveṣṭi* of the elements.
To the east of the *havirdhāna* shed and to the west of the *āhavanīya* fire, he spreads a black antelope skin with its neck toward the east and the hairy side upward.

Upon it the sacrificer sits, turned toward the east, having made a lap. With the formula, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ... (1.7.10h1), he sprinkles him from the front, facing westward, from the head, using a ladle (*sruva*) made of *udumbara* wood. "A—"
"I sprinkle you with the Aśvins, with Sarasvatī, with the impulse of speech... (as in the same source until the end)—thus for a Brāhmaṇa;
"With the sovereignty of Indra I sprinkle you"—thus for a Rājanya;
"With the [sovereignty] of Bṛhaspati I sprinkle you"—thus for a king.
He consecrates him with everything [of the mixture], letting it flow down as far as the mouth;
he offers six oblations of *pārtha* wood; the *aveṣṭi* sacrifice of the elements consists of six [oblations], beginning with "To Indra, svāhā!"—these are the *pārtha* oblations.
With the formula, “To the waters, svāhā! (1.8.13i7), he performs the *aveṣṭi* sacrifice for the elements;
with “Night and Dawn” (4.7.12h,1?), he offers the milk of a black cow that has a white calf using a cup; and with “The giver of wealth, svāhā!
(ibid., to the end, with *svāhā*) and “The upholder of truth, the establisher of truth” (*Ṛtāṣāḍ ṛtadhāmā*, 3.4.7.1a,1p), he offers the six *rāṣṭrabhṛt* oblations (ibid. a–f).

With the mantra, “O Lord of the World” (3.4.7.2g,1), he offers five identical oblations while the chariot is held facing westward above the fire at its front. Taking the *sruva* ladle in his joined palms with the mantra, “Thou art the ocean, full of moisture” (4.7.12.3i1,1), he offers three oblations with the names of the winds, beginning with, “The giver of moisture, the source of bliss—blow, svāhā! (ibid., end of section i3).
He offers five *arka* oblations with the formulas: “*śuvar na gharmas svāhā*” (5.7.5b1), and “*śuvar nārka=sūryās svāhā*” (ibid. b2–b5).
He offers the oblation to Varuṇa with the verse beginning “*tat tvā yāmi*” (4.2.11s; cf. 2.1.11w; 2.5.12m[p]; 5.7.6e[p]), ending with “*brahmaṇā pramokṣīṣva svāhā*” (ibid., with *svāhā*).

He offers three *ruca* oblations with the verses: "O Agni, those splendors of yours which are in the sun... (5.7.6d1,1), followed by: "...rising from the sky... svāhā; O gods, that which is yours... Bṛhaspati, svāhā; shining, bestow upon us... with splendor, splendor, svāhā" (5.7.6d1–d3, with *svāhā* at the end of each respectively).
Then he offers three *agnihotra* oblations with the formula: "Agni is light... (?), namely: "Light is Agni, svāhā;
Indra is light, light is Indra, svāhā; Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya, svāhā" (?).
"Whatever flowed from intention" (5.7.7a,1)—with these ten verses he releases them; of these, he releases one.
<52> At this point, they turn back at the two *havirdhāna* sheds.
When the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths have been strewn, the ritual action succeeds for those who occupy the *dhiṣṇiyas*. He takes the fire into himself and releases it:

with the verse, "O Agni, may splendor be mine in the invocations" (4.7.14.1a), he places one brick on the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth, saying, "And we, kindling thee with ghee, may we conquer through truth... sit down" (4.7.14a, with the *t* mantra).

With the formula, "Fill the world" (VS 4.2.4), he lays down eleven *lokaṃpṛṇā* bricks; with the mantra, "They, yielding milk for him... (VS 10.19), and with "The consciousness and the unconsciousness... (VS 5.5.4.4), he touches [the altar].
With the verse, "He was asked in heaven" (4.4.12.5q; 1.5.11d; #TB 3.7.11.6), he touches the loose earth (*purīṣa*).

With the formula, "The thought, the non-thought" (5.5.4.4,1), and "Sit down by means of that" (the *t*-mantra), and with "May all the gods be present at my invocation" (4.7.14b,1), he places one brick on the *dhishṇya* of the Hotṛ-priest, saying: "O you who possess Indra, [be present] at this desire... sit down by means of that" (the same formula, with the *t*-mantra).

With the formula, "Fill the world" (4.2.4n,1), he lays down eleven *lokaṃpṛṇā* bricks. With the mantra, "They, yielding milk for him" (*tā asya sūdadohasaḥ*), and with "The thought and the non-thought" (5.5.4.4,1), he touches [the altar]. With "He is praised in heaven" (4.4.12q[p]; 1.5.11d; #TB3.7.11.6), he scatters the loose earth (*purīṣa*).

He touches [the brick] with the words, "Consciousness and unconsciousness" (5.5.4.4,1). With the mantra, "Sit down by means of that," and with the words, "May the gods bestow wealth upon me" (4.7.14.1c,1), he places one brick on the *dhiṣṇya* of the Maitrāvaruṇa. With the words, "May there be a blessing for me...

[and] excellent heroes" (*ibid.* to the end), and with the mantra, "Sit down by means of that," and with the words, "Fill the space" (4.2.4n,1)—[he places the bricks] with the formula, "Sit down sevenfold" (*ibid.*, see above for abbreviation).

With the formula, "Let them sacrifice for me; let my oblations be mine" (4.7.14.2d, 1), he places one brick on the *dhiṣṇiya* of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with the mantra: "May my intention be true... speak it for me" (ibid., end) and "sit upon that" (4.7.14.2d).
Then, with the formula "Fill the space" (4.2.4n, 1) and "Sit firm" (K4, 65b12), he places seven bricks.

With the formula, "O Goddesses, six wide ones" (4.7.14.2e, 1), he places one brick on the *dhiṣṇya* of the *Potṛ* priest, [reciting] "Make wide space for us, O King Soma... sit upon it" (with the *t*-mantra).
With "Fill the space" (4.2.4n, 1), [he places another];

with "Sit upon it," and "Agni, driving away wrath... (4.7.14.2–3f, 1), he places [bricks] on the *dhiṣṇya* of the *Neṣṭṛ* priest, [reciting] "...uninjured from the front... may he not perish; sit upon it" (4.7.14f, with the *t*-mantra).

With the verse, “The Ordainer of the ordainers” (4.7.14.3g), he places one brick on the *dhiṣṇya* altar of the Acchāvāka, saying: “He who is the lord of the world... the sacrificer has taken his place... with that [brick], sit down! (4.7.14g, with the *t*-mantra).

With the verse, “May the wide-striding buffalo grant us protection” (4.7.14h), he places one brick on the *mārjālīya* *dhiṣṇya*, saying: “In this invocation... do not abandon me... with that [brick], sit down! (4.7.14h, with the *t*-mantra). He then lays down five *lokaṃpṛṇā* bricks.
With the formula, “*tā asya sīda*,” [the Adhvaryu]...
(15) ...in all [the rites], the *anuvāka*... (4) ...is successfully accomplished; [this applies] from the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*) of the Agniṣomīya sacrifice.

"Offer the oblations for Agni... (16?)... for the sake of..."—these eight are the oblations for the *pṛṣṭhya* [stotra], beginning with "For Agni, who is associated with the *gāyatrī*, the *trivṛt*, and the *rāthaṃtara*" (7.5.14.1). There are ten [formulas] including the *praiṣa*. For the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*), [the Adhvaryu says] "Recite! and "Sacrifice!"; for the other oblations, [the recitation and sacrifice are performed] in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
The *praiṣavān* and *sviṣṭakṛt* offerings are identical; likewise, the *iḍā* is identical when the *iḍā* has been invoked. [He recites:
"May Savitṛ impel you among the impellers... and so on, up to "...of names" (1.8.10.1–2b).
Then, with the verse, "O gods who are god-impellers," he takes hold of his right hand (1.8.10c,1), saying, "He, the son of such-and-such, is the king of the Brāhmaṇas" (1.8.10c-d).
Having stepped forth with the Viṣṇu-strides, [reciting] "Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu; thou art the step of Viṣṇu" (ŚB 1.8.10.2g), they dwell [therein];
the rite is accomplished through the laying of the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*);
he lays down the enclosing-sticks made of *udumbara* wood.
The *mahā-ṛṣi*... (10) causes the sacrificer to recite the *yajus* formulas;
he touches the two *audumbara* [posts] with the *anuvākyās*;

he yokes the fire with three [verses], beginning with "I yoke Agni with power and ghee" (4.7.13.1a, 1); the Adhvaryu touches the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) with [the verses] "The divine eagle, by his strength... and "Do not harm me" (4.7.13a–d1).
The morning pressing succeeds; the midday pressing succeeds;
the *nārāśaṃsa* cups are set down; when the *nārāśaṃsa* cups have been set down, [he offers] a golden vessel with the verse: "The face of the gods has risen... (TS 1.4.43.1b).
At midday, during the fullness of spring, he causes the horse to smell [the offering] with the mantra, "The eye of Mitra... [and of all that stands]" (RV 7.61.1–3).
He gives this gold and the horse to the Brahman priest.
Thus the midday pressing is successfully accomplished.

The third *savana* is successfully accomplished up until the chanting of the *yajñāyajñiya* stotra. When the *yajñāyajñiya* stotra has been introduced with one [verse], the Pratiprasthātṛ touches the middle enclosing-stick (*paridhi*) with two verses: "Thou standest at the head of the universe, resting" (TS 4.7.13.2d–e) and "In the ocean is thy heart... obeisance to the paths" (end of e).
Thus the ritual action is successfully accomplished up until the *samiṣṭayajus* offerings.

With the verse, “Suck this milk-yielding breast of the waters” (TS 5.5.10.6e), he offers a ladle full of clarified butter before the *samiṣṭayajus* offerings, saying, “O Agni, enter [it] when it is full; *svāhā*” (ibid., ending with *svāhā*).
The ritual procedure for the *anūbandhya* animal sacrifice is thus completed.
Following the *paśupuroḍāśa* of the *anūbandhya*, he prepares the *āmikṣā* curd-mixture dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa together with the *paśupuroḍāśa* of the *anūbandhya*.

For this [offering], the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation is identical to that of the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*), including the calls for the *praiṣas*; the *iḍā* is the same; and when the enclosing sticks (*paridhis*) have been scattered, there is the *vājina* (curd-mixture).

Its consumption is performed with the formula: "That seed of yours which is poured forth, where it settles—of that of yours, which has been drunk by the *vājins*, which is honeyed, and for which we have called for permission, I, having been permitted, partake.
Thus the ritual action is completed up to the *pravrājanas*.

"One should worship with the *āpti* verses," they say, when one is about to go forth into the wandering life (*pravrajati*). [He recites] the nine mantras beginning with "O Agni, you who have entered with the mind" (*āpan tvāgne manasā*) and ending with "The fires belonging to the soil" (*ye 'gnayaḥ purīṣyāḥ*). Having recited the hymn (*uktha*) addressed specifically to Agni, he goes forth, concluding with "Having entered the earth for the sake of life, O Heaven...
(*praviṣṭāḥ pṛthivīm jīvātave suvaḥ*).
If it is an Agniṣṭoma,
he prepares this very Brahmaudana; if it is an Ukthya or a Trirātra, on the following day he prepares the Brahmaudana and pours the residue of the Vasordhārā over it.
These four great officiating priests (mahartvij) eat it;
he gives them four milch-cows.
The piling of the fire-altar (agnicityā) is completed; the piling of the fire-altar is completed.
